item.title: Adviser urges specific complaints over excessive electricity, fuel bills
item.description:
Information and Broadcasting Adviser Dr Zahed Ur Rahman has urged citizens to submit specific complaints with relevant details to the authorities over excessive electricity and fuel bills, rather than making general allegations.
He made the call during a weekly briefing at the Press Information Department’s conference room at the Secretariat on Tuesday.
He said citizens facing excessive bills should first submit a written complaint to the relevant local authority. If the authority refuses to accept the complaint or fails to provide a remedy, that should also be clearly reported.
Zahed said similar complaints had been received in the past and necessary action was taken after verification.
He said he had discussed the issue with the energy minister and that the Ministry of Power, Energy & Mineral Resources was willing to seriously examine complaints regarding excessive bills.
He added that the ministry was committed to ensuring proper redress for citizens and would take necessary action after verifying specific complaints.

item.title: Legal notice seeks halt to risky parasailing in Cox's Bazar
item.description:
A legal notice has been served on the government, demanding an immediate halt to what it described as unsafe and high-risk parasailing operations on Cox's Bazar beach, legal action against the operators concerned, and the introduction of a strict regulatory framework for adventure tourism activities.
The notice was sent by Supreme Court lawyer Advocate Nishat Farzana on Tuesday.
It follows the death of a tourist who fell while parasailing at Darianagar beach in the Himchhari area of Cox's Bazar on August 1.
Describing the incident as "extremely tragic and heartbreaking," the notice says it highlights serious lapses in tourist safety and argues that the authorities cannot avoid responsibility for the incident.
According to the notice, several private operators have been conducting parasailing on Cox's Bazar beach without adequate safety measures, trained personnel or standard equipment. It alleges that despite previous accidents, authorities failed to ensure effective monitoring and regulation.
The notice further states that following the latest incident, officials acknowledged that the operator did not have permission to conduct parasailing activities. At the same time, the administration claimed tourist magistrates were on round-the-clock duty and that the incident occurred without their knowledge.
"The continuation of such unauthorised and risky activities despite the administration's responsibility to oversee them demonstrates administrative failure and raises serious concerns about the safety of future tourists," the notice says.
The notice calls for the immediate suspension of all risky parasailing activities in Cox's Bazar, verification of operators' licences, approvals and safety standards, and the formation of an independent committee to investigate the recent accident. It also demands legal action against those responsible, stronger monitoring by tourist police and tourist magistrates, appropriate compensation for the victim's family, and public disclosure of the action taken against Fly Air Sea Sports Parasailing at Dariyanagar. In addition, it urges the government to formulate and strictly enforce international-standard safety guidelines and a comprehensive regulatory framework for all adventure tourism activities, including parasailing.
The notice asks the authorities to take action within 15 working days, warning that legal proceedings will be initiated in the public interest if no action is taken.

item.title: 20-metre road stays underwater for eight months in Kushtia
item.description:
For nearly eight to ten months every year, crossing a barely 20-metre stretch of road becomes an ordeal for thousands of people in Kumarkhali upazila of Kushtia.
Submerged under knee-deep water for most of the year, the road beneath a British-era railway tunnel in Hatisako area has become a symbol of chronic neglect, disrupting daily life for nearly 100,000 residents of Koya and Nandalalpur unions.
What was once a vital transport link has gradually turned into a bottleneck, with poor drainage and unplanned land filling trapping rainwater for months at a time.
Every monsoon, the road disappears beneath stagnant water. Schoolchildren roll up their uniforms and carry their bags over their heads. Office-goers wade through the murky water before beginning their workday. Easy-bikes and vans frequently break down midway, leaving passengers stranded.
A recent visit to the area found knee-deep water covering both approaches to the tunnel, forcing commuters to navigate the flooded road on foot or risk damaging their vehicles.
For many residents, this is not an occasional inconvenience but a reality they have endured for years.
According to Koya Union Parishad Chairman Md Ali Hossain, the road serves as the only direct route to the upazila headquarters for around 70,000 people in his union.
"The water has nowhere to go because there is no drainage system," he said.
He explained that raising the road level is not a practical solution, as vehicles would then struggle to pass through the low-clearance railway tunnel.
"What was built during the British period has now become a source of suffering in modern times," he said, alleging that repeated appeals to the authorities have produced little progress.
Residents said the railway tunnel was constructed during British rule to maintain communication across the area.
For decades, rainwater naturally drained through surrounding lowlands into nearby wetlands. But over the last ten years, many of those open spaces have been filled to build houses, shops and other structures.
With the natural drainage channels blocked and no engineered drainage system in place, rainwater now accumulates around the tunnel and remains there for months.
By the time the stagnant water begins to recede, another rainy season often arrives.
The prolonged waterlogging has also taken a financial toll on transport operators.
Easy-bike driver Raja Ali said the flooded road frequently damages vehicle batteries and motors.
"The battery gets short-circuited, and the motor is damaged. I spend between Tk5,000 and Tk7,000 every month on repairs," he said.
Many drivers avoid the route altogether, forcing passengers to walk through the flooded section or take longer alternative roads.
For schoolchildren, the flooded road has become a barrier to education.
Umme Maria, a ninth-grade student at Alauddin Nagar Secondary School, said she used to cycle to school before the road became regularly submerged.
"One day I fell because the damaged road was hidden beneath the water. Now I walk or travel by van," she said.
Another student, seventh-grader Huzaifa Rahman, said he has no choice but to walk through the water every day.
"My books, notebooks and school uniform often get wet. Sometimes I cannot even attend classes. It is affecting my studies," he said.
Those unwilling to wade through the flooded road must travel an additional three to four kilometres using alternative routes.
Pedestrians Rezaul Islam and Md Shantu said the detour increases both travel time and transportation costs.
"We need a planned solution instead of temporary fixes," they said.
Sixty-five-year-old farmer Bishu Sikder recalled a time when the area was surrounded by open land.
"Earlier, rainwater flowed through highway pipes into nearby wetlands," he said.
"Now people have filled the land to build houses and shops. There is simply no outlet for the water."
Nearby resident Rozina Khatun said water begins accumulating during the monsoon and often remains until the Bengali months of Chaitra and Baishakh.
"Before the water dries up completely, the rains return again. The road stays underwater for more than eight months every year," she said.
Engineer Md Nazmul Haque of Kumarkhali Upazila LGED, acknowledged the drainage problem, saying the area lacks any proper drainage infrastructure.
According to him, resolving the waterlogging would require constructing a culvert on the adjacent highway to allow water to flow out, a project beyond the jurisdiction of the Local Government Engineering Department (LGED).
Upazila Nirbahi Officer Farzana Akhter said the administration is discussing the matter with higher authorities.
She expressed hope that a planned development project could be undertaken once the necessary approvals and funding are secured.
Until then, however, a road measuring only 20 metres continues to test the patience—and resilience—of thousands of people every single day.

item.title: How to book tickets for July Uprising Museum
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman is set to inaugurate the July Uprising Memorial Museum on Wednesday. The museum will be reserved exclusively for family members of those killed in the July movement on the opening day.
Culture Minister Nitai Roy Chowdhury said the museum will open to the general public from Thursday. Visitors will have to purchase tickets to enter.

item.title: Shafique, Babar lead strong Pakistan reply against West Indies
item.description:
Abdullah Shafique struck his sixth Test century and Babar Azam closed in on a hundred as Pakistan reached 266-2 in reply to West Indies' 344 on day two of the second Test in Trinidad on Monday.
Just days after flying into the Caribbean as an emergency replacement, Shafique ended the day unbeaten on 107 off 185 balls with 10 fours and two sixes decorating his authoritative innings at Queen's Park Oval.
Babar, the only visitor to emerge with any credit from a disastrous second innings of the first Test when he finished unbeaten on 58, was again unbowed on 86.
His calm, classy innings has so far occupied 126 deliveries, embellished by 10 fours and one six.
Putting aside those batting woes of a 90-run loss at the Brian Lara Stadium a few miles away, captain Babar and the recalled Shafique made the most of ideal batting conditions and pleasant weather, gathering runs in style in an unbroken third-wicket stand of 168.
Recalled after Shan Masood's finger injury, Shafique looked at ease in the unfamiliar position of number three when he replaced Imam-ul-Haq, who was dismissed by Shamar Joseph.
It was his first opportunity since losing his place after the South Africa series at home last October.
He put on 64 attractive runs with Azan Awais, the opener flaying 10 fours in a 71-ball 55 before being adjudged lbw on television review to left-arm spinner Jomel Warrican.
Babar got into stride almost immediately and with the West Indies hampered by the unavailability of first Test match-winner Justin Greaves with a leg injury and captain Roston Chase ineffective with his off-spinners because of a lacerated finger, the tourists' task was made that bit easier.
- Shafique grabs opportunity -
Yet nothing could take away from the excellence of their strokeplay and the manner in which they dominated an attack that had them on their knees six days earlier when they crashed to 71 for nine, eventually being dismissed for 120 in the last innings of the first Test.
"Their partnership has been quite remarkable and that's just the thing we have been missing in the last two-three Test matches," said delighted batting coach and former Pakistan international batsman Asad Shafique.
"Abdullah has been scoring heavily in domestic competition and he has taken this opportunity with both hands. For me, the hallmark of his innings was the way he put away the bad deliveries and respected the good ones."
Babar, who continues to face severe criticism for what is seen as a rather passive style of leadership, was in his element with bat in hand though, playing a vital guiding role in ensuring that Shafique stayed focused.
When Shafique reached his century shortly before stumps, pulling a short ball to the midwicket boundary, Babar celebrated warmly with the 26-year-old.
Earlier, West Indies extended their first innings by 109 runs in the elongated morning session but that effort was put into context by the ease with the Pakistani top-order gathered runs in reply.
All-rounder Greaves and overnight partner Chase pushed their sixth-wicket stand to 96 before the summoning of the second new ball, unexpectedly in the hands of spinner Ali Usman, brought the breakthrough when Greaves, on 73, sliced an ambitious heave to point.
Fast-medium bowler Ubaid Shah then bowled Chase for 70 and despite more typically stubborn resistance from Kemar Roach, Sajid Khan claimed the last three wickets, the off-spinner finishing with the best figures of four for 85.

item.title: Experts discuss food choices to improve nutrition interventions in Bangladesh
item.description:
Food and nutrition experts from government, academia, civil society, the food and restaurant industry, youth organizations and the CGIAR gathered in Dhaka on Tuesday to identify opportunities for nutrition interventions that support healthier and more sustainable diets.
The Expert Elicitation Workshop, organized by the International Rice Research Institute (IRRI) at the Sheraton Dhaka, used a structured expert elicitation process to examine the factors influencing what, why and when people eat.
The workshop brought together 39 experts from organizations including the Bangladesh Agricultural Research Council, Bangladesh Agricultural University, the Aga Khan Academy, Brac James P Grant School of Public Health, Daffodil International University, the University of Dhaka, Noakhali Science and Technology University, Alive & Thrive Bangladesh, Bangladesh Diabetic Network Ltd, Brac Health Program, GAIN Bangladesh, SAJIDA Foundation, SUN Bangladesh Youth Network, Doehler Group Bangladesh, the International Food Policy Research Institute (IFPRI), IRRI and representatives from restaurant businesses.
Youth representatives, a food historian and food vloggers also participated, offering perspectives on traditional Bangladeshi cuisine, evolving food culture and changing dietary patterns.
The workshop aimed to generate evidence on the cultural, social, economic and behavioural factors shaping food choices in Bangladesh under the Gastronomic Systems Research (GSR) framework.
Discussions focused on commonly consumed foods across different eating occasions, cultural and social influences on diets, food affordability, seasonal food availability, food environments and purchasing behaviour, barriers to healthier diets and opportunities for nutrition interventions.
According to the organizers, expert elicitation is increasingly recognised as an effective method for generating evidence where empirical data is limited or where timely information is needed to support research and policymaking.
Opening the workshop, Dr Arindam Samaddar, project leader at IRRI, said improving diets is not only about producing more food but also about understanding why people choose the foods they eat.
"Food choices are shaped by culture, affordability, availability, convenience and personal preferences. By understanding these everyday decisions, we can design nutrition interventions that are more relevant, practical and likely to improve people's diets," he said.
"If diets are culturally shaped, interventions must also be culturally designed."
Dr Humnath Bhandari, IRRI representative for Bangladesh, said health and nutrition are central to IRRI's new strategy, reflecting the institute's commitment to promoting rice-based food systems that improve both food security and nutrition.
Dr Hafizur Rahman Bhuiyan, associate professor at the Department of Food Engineering and Technology at Bangladesh Agricultural University, said the GSR framework offers a practical and sustainable approach to addressing complex nutrition challenges.
"The GSR framework is simple, effective and sustainable. It provides a practical way to address complex nutrition challenges through interventions grounded in people's everyday food choices. This approach has the potential to create meaningful, real-life impact by informing solutions that are relevant, scalable and responsive to local contexts," he said.
Israt Jahan Dorin, chief dietitian at Bangladesh Diabetic Network Ltd, said understanding the cultural drivers of food choice is essential for tackling the growing burden of diet-related diseases.
"I believe understanding the cultural drivers of food choice is fundamental to designing effective diabetes prevention and nutrition interventions. By recognising how culture, traditions and everyday food practices influence dietary decisions, we can develop interventions that are practical, culturally appropriate and more likely to improve health outcomes," she said.

item.title: Amorim evokes spirit of Baresi as he bids to revive Milan fortunes
item.description:
New AC Milan coach Ruben Amorim vowed on Tuesday to honour the legacy of club legend Franco Baresi, who died last week, as he sets about reviving the fortunes of the ailing Italian giants.
Portuguese Amorim has returned to coaching after being sacked in January by Manchester United and faces a Milan derby against bitter rivals Inter in the Western Australia city of Perth on Wednesday.
Amorim's reign began with a 2-2 draw in a friendly against Celtic in Glasgow last month.
The 41-year-old's immediate target will be a top-four finish in Serie A after AC Milan missed out on the Champions League on the final day of last season.
"I feel that the group is really together," Amorim told reporters in Perth.
"The important thing is to continue with this spirit when things become difficult.
"In this club you need to win every game, so we need to keep that spirit all season."
AC Milan were boosted in the close season by veteran midfield maestro Luka Modric agreeing a one-year contract extension.
- Emotional occasion - Amorim said Modric would play against Inter, having just competed at his fifth World Cup where Croatia were knocked out in the last 32 by Portugal.
"We did a lot to get him back at least for one more year," Amorim said of the former Tottenham and Real Madrid star, who turns 41 in September.
"I'm really pleased with him and he is ready to play some minutes tomorrow."
The match will be an emotional first match for AC Milan since the death of Baresi, who captained the club during a golden era in the 1980s and 1990s.
"When you talk with all the staff about Franco, you see the tears in their eyes," Amorim said.
"Franco was all about the team. The team is the most important thing in our club.
"I will not promise results, but I can promise that I will continue the legacy of Franco."
AC Milan will continue their pre-season against Chelsea in Jakarta on Saturday, while Inter Milan -- who beat Manchester City on penalties in Hong Kong on Saturday -- will remain in Perth to play Juventus on the same day.
Juventus round out the series of all-Italian Perth friendlies against Serie B team Palermo on August 11.
The week-long festival, dubbed "Calcio Italiano", comes after a proposed Serie A match between AC Milan and Como in Perth earlier this year was cancelled because of sanctions imposed by the Asian Football Confederation.

item.title: BCB to commercialize domestic tournaments under new reform plan
item.description:
The Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) has undertaken a series of initiatives to make its domestic tournaments more competitive and commercially attractive, while significantly reducing operational costs.
Tournament Committee Chairman Sirajuddin Mohammad Alamgir said the planned reforms could save the BCB between Tk 15 crore and Tk 30 crore annually, with the savings to be redirected towards cricket development.
According to Alamgir, the BCB currently spends more than Tk. 50 crore each year in organizing domestic tournaments, a figure he believes can be substantially reduced through better planning and commercialization.
"From what we have seen, the BCB spends a huge amount of money to run its tournaments. With some well-planned initiatives, we can significantly reduce those costs," Alamgir told the BSS in an exclusive interview.
"After consulting with the board president, we have undertaken several projects regarding our domestic competitions. We have already discussed the plans with our stakeholders, and the results will be visible very soon," he added.
Alamgir, a veteran cricket organizer from Chattogram, said the board is no longer interested in continuing to bear the full financial burden of tournaments such as the National Cricket League (NCL) T20, the Bangladesh Cricket League (BCL) four-day and one-day competitions.
Under the proposed model, the BCB plans to market the BCL four-day, BCL one-day and NCL T20 tournaments as a single commercial package. Each competition will feature six privately owned teams, with approximately 60 days allocated for the combined schedule.
The traditional eight-team NCL four-day championship, however, will continue in its existing format with divisional teams, alongside a three-day NCL Second XI competition.
"If we continue these tournaments in the conventional way, they will not benefit us financially. That's why we have decided to market them. The money we save through effective cost-cutting can later be invested in development projects," Alamgir said.
"We have already shared our ideas with the marketing department to explore how domestic cricket can be marketed more effectively."
Alamgir believes improved marketing will not only generate greater revenue for the BCB but also enhance the competitiveness and appeal of the domestic competitions.
He also dismissed concerns over possible payment complications under the proposed ownership model.
"The owners will not have to pay franchise fees like those in the Bangladesh Premier League (BPL). They will simply follow the existing payment structure that the BCB uses for players in tournaments such as the BCL and NCL.
Therefore, there will be no payment-related complications, while the board will save a significant amount of money," he said.
"These tournaments are marketable products. I find it hard to believe that the cricket board cannot sell its own competitions.
If we can properly demonstrate the commercial opportunities to our sponsors, I believe we will be able to market these events successfully. Discussions have already begun, and the results will be seen very soon."
He added that successful commercialization would also allow the BCB to pay players in advance, eliminating the recurring problem of delayed payments.
"There is no need to charge a huge ownership fee. The owners would simply need to advance the players' payments under the existing first-class payment structure or any other structure already in place," he added.
Alamgir also revealed plans to introduce foreign players into the domestic competitions through a player exchange programme. "The exchange programme will reduce the cost of bringing foreign players in."
"At the same time, it will make our competitions more competitive and attractive. Our local players will benefit immensely from sharing dressing rooms with overseas cricketers. Likewise, our players will also participate in tournaments abroad under the programme, gaining valuable international exposure."
In addition, the BCB is planning to introduce two new competitions to strengthen the country's talent pipeline: a Rising Star tournament for Under-23 cricketers and an Inter-University Cricket League.
"We are planning to include the Rising Star competition and the Inter-University Cricket League in the domestic calendar. We believe these tournaments will further strengthen our player development pathway, and we are committed to implementing them," Alamgir said.
He also confirmed that district-level cricket competitions will be held in phases, with each district receiving Tk. 5 lakh in financial support from the BCB.
"In the first phase, competitions will be held in 20 districts, and we have already sent official letters in this regard. Another 20 districts will host their tournaments in the second phase, while the remaining 24 districts will organize their competitions in the final phase," he said.

item.title: Osaka out to improve Toronto fortunes with eye on US Open
item.description:
Naomi Osaka is hoping her success last year in Montreal, where she finished runner-up to Victoria Mboko, will translate as the WTA's 1000 event in Canada shifts to Toronto.
The four-time Grand Slam champion from Japan is coming off a semi-final run on the hard courts of Washington, where she fell to eventual champion Alexandra Eala of the Philippines.
"I did better than last year in DC, so I'm just hoping to keep the ball rolling," Osaka said.
"I haven't historically played super, super well here, so I'm just hoping to change that this year.
"I can try to recall Montreal, but I would like to kind of treat the cities separately," added Osaka, whose best run in Toronto -- which alternates hosting duties with Montreal each year -- was a quarter-final appearance back in 2019.
The former world number one is seeded 11th this year and aiming to build momentum as the August 31 start of the US Open approaches.
Osaka earned the last of her four major titles at the 2021 Australian Open and has yet to regain the heights she reached before taking an extended maternity leave in 2023.
But she made it to the US Open semi-finals last year and reached the last 16 at the French Open for the first time this year before a career-best quarter-final at Wimbledon.
"I would just hope to gain a lot of confidence leading into New York," she said.
"I lost my last match, but it's helped me figure out what I want to do exactly, or how I want to take my tennis."
Osaka is in the same quarter as second-seeded Australian Open champion Elena Rybakina and in the fourth round she could find herself up against fifth-seeded French Open champion Mirra Andreeva.
Andreeva, who suffered a shock second-round exit at Wimbledon, will face a tricky opening match against former world number one Karolina Pliskova, who beat Ukraine's Oleksandra Oliynykova 6-4, 6-4 on Monday.
Osaka will open against Hungary's Panna Uvardy, who was up 2-6, 7-6 (7/3), 2-0 against Eva Lys when the German retired because of injury in a match in which she led the second set 5-2.
It was a jam-packed schedule on the second day of first-round play.
Among the winners, Poland's Magdalena Frech defeated France's Leolia Jeanjean 7-5, 6-3 to line up a meeting with third-seeded two-time champion Jessica Pegula.
Pegula beat Frech last week on the way to the final in Washington, where the American fell to Eala in the rain-delayed title match on Monday.
In other early matches, American Kayla Day beat Diane Parry of France 3-6, 6-3, 7-5 to book a clash with fourth-seeded Coco Gauff.
World number one Aryna Sabalenka is the top seed in the tournament.
After disappointing runs at the French Open and Wimbledon the Belarusian is aiming to reassert her dominance on hard courts, where her lone defeat this year was to Rybakina in the Australian Open final.

item.title: Chhatra Dal activists remain outside National Medical Institute Hospital; Police on alert
item.description:
Chhatra Dal activists remain outside National Medical Institute Hospital; Police on alert

Chhatra Dal leaders and activists were still gathered outside National Medical Institute Hospital in the capital on Tuesday evening. However, no leaders or activists of Islami Chhatra Shibir were seen at the scene. Police remained on alert.

Earlier in the day, people injured in the clashes involving Chhatra Dal, Islami Chhatra Shibir, and Jatiya Chhatra Shakti at Jagannath University were reportedly assaulted after they arrived at the emergency department of National Medical Institute Hospital for treatment. The incident heightened tensions outside the hospital.

Kotwali Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Rabiul Islam told Prothom Alo in the evening that the situation was now calm and that those who had been receiving treatment had been transferred to another hospital.

He added that leaders and activists of Chhatra Dal, Jubo Dal, and the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) were near Kabi Nazrul Government College and Jagannath University, while police remained on high alert.

As of around 6:45 pm, when this report was filed, Chhatra Dal activists were still present outside the hospital alongside police personnel. No Chhatra Shibir leaders or activists were seen there.

Fresh tensions erupt outside National Medical Institute Hospital

Fresh tensions have erupted outside National Medical Institute Hospital following the clashes involving Chhatra Dal, Islami Chhatra Shibir, and Jatiya Chhatra Shakti at Jagannath University.

Leaders and activists from both sides have gathered outside the hospital. Eyewitnesses said leaders and activists of the Dhaka South units of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), Jubo Dal, and Chhatra Dal were also present.

Police have been deployed to the area to keep the situation under control.

Several injured in clash between Chhatra Dal and Chhatra Shibir at Dhaka College

Several people were injured in a clash between activists of the Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal and Islami Chhatra Shibir at Dhaka College, according to police.

Sheikh Zahidul Islam, deputy commissioner of the Ramna Division of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police, told Prothom Alo that the clash took place inside the Dhaka College campus.

"There was a fight between Chhatra Dal and Chhatra Shibir inside the campus. Several people were injured," he said.

He added that police are not stationed inside the campus but responded after receiving information about the incident.

Chhatra Dal and Chhatra Shibir clash at Dhaka College, several injured

Clashes Between Chhatra Dal and Chhatra Shibir Outside Dhaka Alia Madrasa

Supporters of the Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal and Islami Chhatra Shibir are clashing in front of Dhaka Alia Madrasa in the Bakshibazar area of the capital.

The confrontation began at around 5:15 pm on Tuesday in front of the Alia Madrasa field, with both sides chasing each other. Several people have reportedly been injured.

Activists from both groups were seen throwing bricks and engaging in running battles.

Chhatra Dal and JnUCSU–Chhatra Shakti activists clash at Jagannath University

Fresh Attack on Injured Shibir and Chhatra Shakti Leaders at National Medical Institute Hospital

Leaders and activists of Islami Chhatra Shibir and Jatiya Chhatra Shakti who were receiving treatment in the emergency department of National Medical Institute Hospital after the earlier clashes at Jagannath University were reportedly attacked again.

According to the report, leaders and activists of the Dhaka South units of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), Jubo Dal, and Chhatra Dal entered the hospital at around 4:45 pm.

They allegedly assaulted injured activists outside the hospital as well as those undergoing treatment in the emergency department. One injured person was reportedly dragged out of the emergency ward and beaten.

Earlier, a scuffle and subsequent clash broke out between activists of the Bangladesh Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal and leaders and activists of the Jagannath University Central Students' Union (JnUCSU) and Jatiya Chhatra Shakti over entry into a seminar marking the second anniversary of the July Mass Uprising at Jagannath University.

The incidents occurred around noon on Tuesday at the university auditorium and later in front of the Shaheed Minar.

item.title: Content creator Ripon Mia accused of raping schoolgirl; arbitration at BNP office
item.description:
Content creator Ripon Mia has been accused of raping a 14-year-old schoolgirl in Netrakona Sadar upazila. But the matter was settled through arbitration at a local BNP office instead of going to the police and it was decided to fine him Tk 500,000 and expel him from the area.

The arbitration sparked criticism after several videos of the proceedings started circulating on social media. However, police said they are investigating the matter and taking legal action.

Ripon Mia, a carpenter by profession, has been making videos on Facebook since 2016. He came to limelight for videos featuring the catchphrases "Hi, I'm Ripon Video" and "I Love You, Etai Bastob (This Is Reality)." In 2019, he opened a Facebook page named "Ripon Mia," that currently has 1.9 million followers.

The family of the teenage girl alleged that Ripon went to their home around 8:00 PM last Saturday. At that time, the schoolgirl was cooking in the yard of the house. Her father was at a tea shop in the local market and her mother was away at work. Taking advantage of this opportunity, Ripon forcibly took the student to a nearby jungle and raped her. Later, when local people rushed over upon hearing the girl's screams, Ripon fled.

The family claimed that Ripon had been harassing the girl for some time, saying he wanted to make videos with her. Out of fear of social stigma, the family did not disclose the incident at first. Later, after the matter became known in the area, arbitration was held at a local BNP office in a nearby market on Monday night.

A person who attended the arbitration, requesting anonymity, told Prothom Alo that the meeting was led by Fazlur Rahman, former president of the union BNP. Local BNP and Jamaat leaders, along with people from different walks of life, were present at the meeting. During the meeting, Ripon admitted the allegation and apologised. It was later decided to fine him Tk 500,000 and expel him from the area.

Several videos of the arbitration spread on Facebook on Tuesday morning. In one 30-second video, Ripon is seen apologising to everyone present after admitting the allegation. At one point, he says, "Whether I did it or not, I did it. I have to live among you... People make mistakes, and I made one." At one stage, he holds Fazlur Rahman's feet to seek forgiveness.

The videos have sparked criticism. Many people commented that trying a criminal offence such as rape through village arbitration is unlawful.

Pritam Sohag, central coordinator (northern region) of the National Citizen Party (NCP), wrote on Facebook that allegations of rape should be dealt with through the police and the courts in accordance with the law. Attempting to try such a criminal offence at a party office amounts to taking the law into one's own hands and is condemnable, he wrote.

Prothom Alo could not reach Ripon Mia for comment despite repeated attempts, as his mobile phone was switched off. He has gone into hiding after the incident became public.

Speaking to Prothom Alo over mobile phone on Tuesday afternoon, Fazlur Rahman, former president of the union BNP, said, "The girl is from a poor family. After learning about the incident, the girl's family and villagers came to us seeking justice. The family could not afford to pursue a case. We then held arbitration with local residents. Afterwards, we told them to take legal action. It was decided through the arbitration that Tk 500,000 would be paid. Now the police have come and are talking to us."

Officer-in-Charge (OC) of Netrakona Model Police Station Abul Khayer said police went to the scene after learning about the matter through social media. He said the girl had been sent to the police station with her family to file a complaint. Two people who attended the arbitration are being questioned, and efforts are underway to arrest the accused, Ripon Mia.

item.title: Morocco warned Spain after court ruling on migration
item.description:
TOPSHOT-SPAIN-MOROCCO-MIGRATION-CEUTA

Morocco had previously warned Spain that a recent Spanish court ruling that migrants arriving by sea would not face immediate removal was going to create 'a problem,' a senior Moroccan official said.

Last week, at least 50,000 people, mostly Moroccans, entered the Spanish exclave of Ceuta, on foot or by swimming from the nearby city of Fnideq.

This unprecedented influx quickly overwhelmed the Spanish exclave in North Africa, before leading to thousands of returns to Morocco.

Spain's Supreme Court ruled on 8 July that migrants arriving by sea should not be returned as quickly as others and Madrid has blamed criminal gangs for spreading misinformation about the ruling.

"We started engaging with the Spanish side around 22-23 July, when the networks began talking about this," the Moroccan senior official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said on Monday night.

"We discussed this ruling and its impact. We explained that this ruling was going to create a problem. And it did create a problem," he said.

Spanish government spokeswoman Elma Saiz rejected the claim.

"At no point was there any evidence, any report that alerted us to the magnitude of this unprecedented event," she told reporters in Madrid.

The Moroccan official argued the large movement of people into Ceuta was not a failure of Morocco's security apparatus.

"It's simplistic to say that Morocco should just have used force to stop them. That is to completely misunderstand this phenomenon," he said.

"Could Spain, seeing them coming, have done something to stop them simply using weapons and security forces? That's not possible."

"At a certain point, the Moroccan law enforcement forces could no longer confront the migrants because the numbers were very large," and because "the pull effect was very strong," he said.

"It is not Morocco's sole responsibility to manage migration, he said, adding that the cost of migration management for the kingdom amounted to around 500 million euros per year.

He nonetheless said that Rabat and Madrid had acted 'as reliable partners' and continued to work 'in perfect coordination' on migration issues.

"Today, it is up to Spain to find answers to the challenges posed by this ruling," he said.

"Morocco's commitment remains the same. It accepts the return of those who manage to cross. It puts in place preventive measures to stop as many departures as possible, and it will continue" to do so, he said.

Saiz said Spain's "exceptional response in such a short period of time" to the crisis would not have been possible without Morocco's cooperation.

item.title: PM calls for preserving national unity, building democratic Bangladesh
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Tuesday called for maintaining national unity forged during the July-August Mass Uprising and pledged to build a just, democratic and humane Bangladesh by ensuring the political and economic empowerment of the people.
The Head of Government said the student-led mass uprising of August 5, 2024, forced the then government to flee the country, ending what he described as authoritarian rule and renewing the nation's hopes for democracy.
In a message marking the "July Mass Uprising Day" to be observed on Wednesday (August 5), the premier said the day symbolizes "joy, victory and the restoration of democratic political rights" following the end of more than one and a half decades of fascist rule.
Recalling the anti-fascist movement, Tarique Rahman said the BNP, other anti-fascist political parties and people from different walks of life had endured enforced disappearances, killings, abductions, torture, false cases and repression in their struggle to restore democracy and voting rights.
He also paid tribute to former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia, saying the uncompromising leader of the nation had been imprisoned for years on what he described as false charges while leading the democratic movement.
Secret detention centres, known as "Aynaghar", had been established across the country to silence dissent, while many political leaders and activists remained missing, alleged the prime minister.
He said the country's Constitutional and statutory institutions, including the judiciary and the Election Commission, had been rendered ineffective, elections had been reduced to a mere formality, and widespread corruption and money laundering had severely weakened the economy and banking sector.
Highlighting the broad-based participation in the July-August uprising, Tarique Rahman said students, farmers, workers, rickshaw-pullers, day labourers, garment workers, hotel and restaurant employees, transport workers, journalists, intellectuals, cultural activists, professionals, women and people from all sections of the society had joined the movement.
He alleged that security forces opened fire on demonstrators, including from helicopters, resulting in thousands of deaths and injuries.
The premier paid tribute to the martyrs of the movement, including Abu Sayed of Rangpur, Wasim Akram of Chittagong and Mugdho of Dhaka, describing their sacrifices as a lasting source of inspiration for the nation's democratic struggle.
He said thousands were killed and at least 30,000 people were injured during the uprising, while many lost limbs or their eyesight permanently.
On the occasion, Tarique Rahman urged the nation to honour the sacrifices of the martyrs by establishing equality, human dignity and social justice and by building a self-reliant, democratic and humane Bangladesh.
He also called on all pro-democracy political parties and citizens to safeguard national unity despite differences of opinion, saying democracy flourishes through diversity of views, but such differences should never turn into hostility.
The prime minister vowed that autocracy, fascism, extremism and militancy would never again be allowed to take root in Bangladesh, adding that the unity forged through the 2024 mass uprising would remain steadfast.
Drawing a historical parallel, he said 1971 was the struggle to achieve independence, while 2024 was the struggle to safeguard the country's freedom and the rights of its people.

item.title: Home minister: Law and order situation fully under control
item.description:
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed has said that the overall law and order situation in the country is fully under control and that law enforcement agencies are on the highest alert to prevent any kind of subversive activities.
He made the remarks on Tuesday afternoon while responding to various questions from journalists at a press briefing on contemporary issues held at the Ministry of Home Affairs at the secretariat.
The minister said: "Intelligence agencies and law enforcement forces are always active to suppress extremism and maintain internal security."
Responding to a question from journalists about strengthening police security, the minister said that it is a normal practice of the police. "Officers are regularly instructed to ensure that no one remains unattended during patrols or while on duty. There is no reason to interpret it otherwise."
Stating that banned political parties have no scope to carry out any subversive activities, Salahuddin said: "Apart from occasionally peeping through social media from abroad, they have no capacity to make any impact on the ground."
He added: "Appropriate action will be taken after properly investigating the recent incidents involving the NCP."

item.title: PM, Saudi deputy FM agree to deepen strategic partnership
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and Saudi Arabia's Deputy Foreign Minister Eng Waleed El-Khereiji on Tuesday agreed to deepen the longstanding Bangladesh-Saudi Arabia relationship by building a strategic, multidimensional partnership and expanding cooperation in trade, investment, and other key sectors.
The understanding came during a courtesy call by El-Khereiji on the prime minister at the Prime Minister's Office in the Bangladesh Secretariat, according to Prime Minister's Assistant Press Secretary Shahriar Pamir.
Prime Minister Tarique said Bangladesh-Saudi Arabia relations are built on mutual trust and longstanding friendship, adding that his government seeks to develop a strategic, multidimensional, and long-term partnership with the Kingdom.
Inviting greater Saudi investment, the prime minister said Bangladesh offers a conducive environment for investors and particularly encouraged investment in the solar power sector. He noted that the government is implementing extensive programs to expand the use of clean energy and said Saudi investment in the sector would be mutually beneficial.
During the meeting, both sides reaffirmed their commitment to taking bilateral relations to a new level.
El-Khereiji said Bangladesh has created a favorable investment climate under the leadership of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, adding that Saudi Arabia is keen to strengthen ties and expand investment in a range of promising sectors.
He said the Kingdom is interested in investing in Bangladesh's processed food, seafood, tropical fruits, agro-based industries, information technology, artificial intelligence, renewable energy, and other sectors.
The Saudi deputy foreign minister also acknowledged the significant contribution of Bangladeshi workers to Saudi Arabia's development.
El-Khereiji congratulated the prime minister on the election of Bangladesh's Foreign Minister Dr Khalilur Rahman as president of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly.
At the conclusion of the meeting, El-Khereiji invited the prime minister to visit Saudi Arabia. Tarique thanked him for the invitation and expressed hope of visiting the Kingdom at a mutually convenient time.
The Saudi delegation included Adviser to the Interior Minister Lt Gen Sulaiman bin Abdulaziz Al-Yahya, Deputy Minister for Consular Affairs Dr Mohammed Al-Shammari, Deputy Minister of Human Resources and Social Development Muhannad bin Ahmed Al-Issa, Saudi Ambassador to Bangladesh Dr Abdullah bin Abiyah, and senior officials from the Saudi Ministries of Foreign Affairs and Interior.
The Bangladesh side included Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed, Foreign Minister Dr Khalilur Rahman, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed, and the prime minister's adviser on foreign affairs, Humaiun Kobir.

item.title: DMP tightens security across Dhaka ahead of July Mass Uprising day
item.description:
Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) has adopted extensive and multi-layered security measures to maintain law and order and ensure public safety in the capital ahead of July Mass Uprising Day on August 5.
The measures have been taken to prevent any act of sabotage, untoward incident or disruption to public safety during the observance of the day, according to a DMP statement issued on Tuesday.
As part of the security plan, the number of police pickets and checkpoints has been significantly increased across the capital, with stricter search operations at all entry points to Dhaka.
Detective Branch (DB) and Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime (CTTC) personnel in plain clothes will remain deployed at all important venues.
Special sweeping operations will also be conducted by the SWAT, Bomb Disposal Unit and Dog Squad Unit at places expected to witness large public gatherings.
The DMP said all program venues and the July Memorial Monument area have been brought under a special security arrangement, including surveillance through CCTV cameras and drones.
At the same time, intelligence activities by the Counter Terrorism and Intelligence Bureau (CTSB) and Intelligence Analysis Division (IAD) in plain clothes will continue, while an adequate number of Quick Response Teams (QRTs) will remain on standby to respond to any emergency.
In addition to the regular deployment, extra DMP personnel, along with members of the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) and the Criminal Investigation Department (CID), will remain active across the capital to ensure overall security.
Senior police officials will also remain in the field to directly supervise security arrangements throughout the day, the statement added.

item.title: Measles: Death toll stands at 849 as two children die in 24 hours
item.description:
Bangladesh's combined death toll from confirmed and suspected measles cases has risen to 849 after two more children died from measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours until 8:00am on Tuesday, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
The DGHS classified both of the latest fatalities as suspected measles deaths. With the latest update, the number of suspected measles-related deaths has climbed to 753, while laboratory-confirmed measles deaths remained unchanged at 96.
The country also recorded 896 new suspected measles cases during the reporting period, raising the cumulative number of suspected infections to 131,946.
Meanwhile, health authorities confirmed 123 new measles infections through laboratory testing, bringing the total number of confirmed cases nationwide to 16,531.
DGHS data also showed that since March 15, a total of 114,393 patients with suspected measles have been hospitalized across the country. Of them, 110,187 have recovered.

At least two rounds of clashes broke out between activists of Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal (JCD) and Bangladesh Islami Chhatra Shibir at Jagannath University (JnU) on Tuesday, with both groups claiming that more than 50 of their activists and students were injured.
The first clash erupted on the university campus around noon, while the second broke out later outside Dhaka National Medical Institute Hospital, where police intervened to restore order.
Witnesses said the initial clash occurred during a programme marking the July Mass Uprising Day at the university's central auditorium, attended by University Grants Commission (UGC) Chairman Prof Dr Mamun Ahmed as the chief guest.
According to witnesses, Shibir activists entered the venue carrying placards highlighting various student demands, prompting a heated exchange with Chhatra Dal activists that quickly escalated into a clash.
Following the violence, Chhatra Dal activists forced Shibir members off the campus and staged a protest rally.
Around 2:00pm, activists from different units of Chhatra Shibir gathered at Dhaka National Medical Institute Hospital to visit those injured in the earlier clash. At the same time, Chhatra Dal activists assembled outside the hospital's main gate, chanting slogans.
The rival groups again engaged in chases and counter-chases, forcing Shibir activists to take shelter inside the hospital. Witnesses said both sides hurled brickbats at each other, while several individuals were seen carrying locally made weapons.
Jagannath University Central Students' Union (JnUCSU) Vice-President Md Riazul Islam, who is backed by Chhatra Shibir, alleged that Shibir activists had attended the programme with placards to draw the UGC chairman's attention to student demands.
"However, the university administration, several teachers and Chhatra Dal activists prevented us from doing so. At one stage, Chhatra Dal activists attacked us, snatched our placards and assaulted our members, leaving around 50 students injured," he claimed.
Denying the allegation, Chhatra Dal Member Secretary Shamsul Arefin accused Shibir of attempting to divert attention from the alleged failures of the JnUCSU leadership and the activities of Jamaat-Shibir.
"They tried to create mob violence at Jagannath University, similar to what happened at Begum Rokeya University. Since August 5, they have repeatedly promoted mob culture," he alleged.
Jagannath University Vice-Chancellor Professor Dr Md Rais Uddin said a programme marking the July Mass Uprising Day was underway at the auditorium when "a group attempted to create disorder outside."
"We suspect that forces opposed to the July movement may have been involved. We will also investigate whether the Chhatra League had any role in the incident," he said.

item.title: Can a brain implant restore vision? Elon Musk says yes
item.description:
For millions of people living with blindness, the possibility of seeing again has long remained beyond the reach of modern medicine.
Elon Musk now says his brain-chip company Neuralink hopes to change that by developing an implant that bypasses the eyes entirely and sends visual information directly to the brain.
If successful, the technology could mark one of the biggest advances yet in brain-computer interfaces.
But neuroscientists caution that the project remains highly experimental, with no published human data showing that Neuralink’s device can restore vision.
Speaking at a recent public event, Musk said Neuralink plans to begin testing its experimental vision implant, known as Blindsight, in humans after securing the necessary regulatory approvals.
He also repeated his long-term ambition of enabling blind people, including some who have never had functional vision, to perceive images by directly stimulating the brain’s visual cortex.
Those claims, however, remain aspirational rather than clinically proven.
Unlike conventional treatments that attempt to repair the eye, retina or optic nerve, Blindsight is designed to bypass damaged visual pathways altogether.
Tiny implanted electrodes would stimulate the visual cortex, the part of the brain responsible for processing sight, creating artificial visual perception.
The concept itself is not new.
Researchers around the world have been investigating cortical visual prostheses for decades, and several research groups have already demonstrated that direct stimulation of the visual cortex can produce simple flashes of light, known as phosphenes, in blind volunteers.
The challenge has always been transforming those basic light patterns into meaningful, usable vision.
Neuralink believes its high-density brain implant could eventually overcome some of those limitations.
The company received the US Food and Drug Administration’s Breakthrough Device designation for Blindsight in 2024, a status intended to accelerate the review of promising medical technologies for serious conditions.
However, the designation does not mean the device has been proven safe or effective, nor does it constitute regulatory approval for commercial use.
At present, Neuralink’s only publicly registered human clinical study is the PRIME trial, which is evaluating the safety of its brain-computer interface for people with paralysis, allowing them to control computers using neural signals.
No publicly registered human trial has yet demonstrated vision restoration using the Blindsight implant.
That distinction is important because restoring sight is widely regarded as one of neuroscience’s most difficult challenges.
Scientists say vision is not simply a matter of transmitting images into the brain.
The brain must also learn to interpret enormous amounts of complex information, particularly in people who have been blind for many years or since birth.
For that reason, experts say any early success is likely to resemble crude visual perception rather than natural eyesight.
Musk himself has previously acknowledged that the first generation of Blindsight would probably produce only very low-resolution vision before improving over time.
He has also suggested that future versions could eventually surpass normal human eyesight by enabling infrared or ultraviolet perception.
Those enhancement claims remain speculative and have not been demonstrated in scientific studies.
Even so, many neuroscientists view cortical vision research as one of the most promising areas of neurotechnology.
Several academic groups and companies are pursuing similar approaches, reflecting growing confidence that brain-computer interfaces may eventually help restore lost sensory function.
At the same time, researchers emphasize that significant engineering, biological and regulatory hurdles remain before such devices become routine clinical treatments.
For Neuralink, the vision program represents a significant expansion beyond its original focus on restoring communication and computer control for people with paralysis.
Whether Blindsight ultimately fulfils Musk’s ambitious predictions will depend not on public demonstrations or bold announcements, but on carefully conducted human trials, peer-reviewed scientific evidence and long-term safety data.
For now, the promise of restoring sight remains one of the most exciting, and one of the most uncertain, frontiers in modern neuroscience.

item.title: Call for integrated action on climate and early childhood development
item.description:
Policymakers, development experts, and civil society representatives on Tuesday called for coordinated action to address the climate crisis while ensuring children's early development, saying the two priorities are closely interconnected and essential to building a sustainable future.
They urged the government, development partners, civil society, the media, the private sector, and families to work together to safeguard children's wellbeing while protecting the environment.
The call came at a policy dialogue titled What to Do for Childhood: Protecting Childhood and the Earth , jointly organized by the Bangladesh Early Childhood Development Network (BEN) and the Prokriti O Jibon Foundation, with support from Arnec and Somasti Media Communication and Development Foundation. Channel i served as the event's media partner.
Addressing the event as chief guest, Women and Children Affairs Minister Dr AZM Zahid Hossain said investment in early childhood development is one of the country's most important long-term investments rather than an expense.
He said raising public awareness, ensuring adequate financial investment, strengthening policy implementation, and enhancing institutional support are essential to addressing climate change and creating a safe, child-friendly environment. He also stressed the need for close collaboration among the government, development partners, private organizations, the media, and civil society.
Presiding over the event, Prokriti O Jibon Foundation Chairman Mukit Majumder Babu said protecting children's care, development, and wellbeing must go hand in hand with conserving nature, the environment, and biodiversity to leave a livable planet for future generations.
He said investing in children today and protecting the Earth are equally important for building a stronger and more humane society.
Presenting the keynote paper, BEN Vice-President Mahmuda Akter highlighted the importance of the first 1,000 days of a child's life, describing it as the most critical period for physical, cognitive, social, and emotional development.
She said ensuring proper nutrition, healthcare, responsive caregiving, a nurturing family environment, and early learning opportunities during this period significantly improves a child's lifelong potential, calling for increased public and private investment.
The discussion featured representatives from UNICEF Bangladesh, UNESCO, government agencies, universities, and development organizations, including Save the Children Bangladesh, Plan International Bangladesh, Synergos, Manusher Jonno Foundation, BRAC University, Independent University, Bangladesh, North South University, and the Department of Social Services.
Speakers said many families in Bangladesh remain unaware of the importance of early childhood development, resulting in gaps in nutrition, healthcare, quality caregiving, safe environments, and pre-primary education. They stressed the need to raise public awareness, strengthen parental capacity, expand community-level services, and improve community engagement.
They also emphasized that children are among the most vulnerable to the impacts of climate change and called for greater investment in child-centered climate adaptation and sustainable development planning.
The speakers agreed that ensuring children's wellbeing and protecting the environment require stronger coordination among government institutions, development partners, educational institutions, the private sector, the media, and civil society. They urged policymakers to place children's rights, safety, and environmental conservation at the center of national development planning.

item.title: Shibir-JCD clash leaves Dhaka Alia Madrasa principal among 10 injured
item.description:
The principal of Dhaka Alia Madrasa and nine others were injured after activists of Islami Chhatra Shibir and Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal (JCD) clashed on Tuesday afternoon over a dispute involving dormitory seats.
The violence erupted outside the campus, where activists from both groups exchanged brickbats and engaged in several rounds of chases and counter-chases, according to witnesses and campus sources.
Among the injured was the madrasa's principal Mahmud Obaidul Haque, 52, who was rescued by teachers and students and taken to the emergency department of Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH) at around 5:00pm. He is currently undergoing treatment in Ward No 4.
Also injured were Shamim Mahmud, 30, president of JCD's Dhaka South unit; Sanaullah, 30, former senior joint convener of the Government Alia Madrasa unit of JCD; and Nesar Uddin Rabbi, 27, member secretary of Lalbagh Thana JCD. They were later taken to DMCH for treatment.
Sabbir Rahman, who accompanied the injured to the hospital, confirmed their identities.
Inspector Md Faruk, in-charge of the DMCH Police camp, confirmed that the injured are receiving treatment at the hospital. Police rushed to the scene and brought the situation under control, though tension continued to prevail in the area.
Shibir alleged that its activists were attacked after protesting what it described as the illegal occupation of dormitory seats.
JCD, however, claimed that Shibir was deliberately trying to destabilise educational institutions through planned violence.
As of 6:00pm, when this report was filed, the clashes had subsided, but the campus remained tense. Additional police personnel were deployed, and law enforcement agencies continued to monitor the situation.
Chawkbazar Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Md Mamun said the clash occurred outside the campus between activists of JCD and Shibir, leaving several members of both groups injured.
"The situation is now under control, and police have been deployed in the area," he said.
Meanwhile, separate clashes between activists of Islami Chhatra Shibir and JCD also broke out at Jagannath University and Dhaka College on Tuesday, raising fresh concerns over security at educational institutions across the capital.
Dhaka Metropolitan Police Additional Commissioner Osman Gani told DhakaTribune that clashes had occurred at all three campuses. "Police intervened and brought the situations under control. The situation is now normal, and additional personnel have been deployed on the campuses," he said.

item.title: Faridpur DB OC, 10 others face departmental action over Chhatra League man's custodial death
item.description:
An internal investigation by Faridpur district police has recommended departmental proceedings against the then officer-in-charge (OC) of the Detective Branch (DB) and 10 other police personnel over the custodial death of banned Bangladesh Chhatra League (BCL) activist Mirza Ishtiaq Ahmed Pranto.
The report of the probe has already been sent to Police Headquarters for further action, Faridpur Superintendent of Police Shahriar Muhammad Miajee said on Tuesday.
"The internal investigation recommended initiating departmental proceedings against the 11 DB members, including the OC, and taking disciplinary action against them," he told reporters.
Pranto, a resident of West Gondhardia in Madhukhali upazila, was picked up by DB police from in front of his house by the Dhaka-Khulna highway on June 20.
According to police, he fell ill while in DB custody and died at Faridpur Medical College Hospital the following day.
A student of Faridpur Law College, Pranto also worked as a seasonal labourer at Faridpur Sugar Mills.
On June 21, Sub-Inspector Ahaduzzaman, who took part in the operation, filed a narcotics case at Madhukhali Police Station, claiming that 100 grams of cannabis were recovered from Pranto.
According to the case statement, the raid took place around 2am on June 21. During the raid, Pranto admitted possessing the drugs before handing them over from a pocket of his trousers in the presence of two witnesses.
However, a video of the incident that later surfaced appeared to show the operation taking place during daylight, with Pranto wearing a lungi instead of trousers.
The two witnesses named in the case also told investigators that they were not present at the scene during the recovery and signed documents later after being misled and intimidated.
Pranto's mother Khadija Akter alleged that DB personnel demanded Tk65,000 for her son's release on the night of his detention and later asked her to bring Tk100,000 the following morning.
She said she arrived with the money but received her son's body instead.
As the news drew huge flak, the district police formed a three-member internal investigation committee headed by Additional Superintendent of Police (Administration and Finance) Fatema Islam.
The committee also included Additional Superintendent of Police (Crime and Operations) Md Shamsul Azam and district Special Branch OC Mosharraf Hossain.
SP Miajee said the probe found that all officers involved in the operation had some level of responsibility and recommended a departmental investigation to determine each individual's role before further action is taken.
He, however, declined to comment on specific inconsistencies surrounding the case, including the drug recovery, discrepancies over the timing of the operation, the presence of the witnesses and allegations that money was demanded from the victim's family.
Following the incident, the then DB OC and the 10 other police personnel involved in the operation were attached to the Faridpur Police Lines.

item.title: Two madrasa teachers sent to jail in student murder case
item.description:
A Dhaka court on Tuesday sent two madrasa teachers to jail in a murder case filed over the death of a 13-year-old student whose body was recovered from a washroom at a madrasa in the capital's Kadamtali area.
Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Hasibuzzaman passed the order after the investigation officer produced the accused before the court and sought their detention pending investigation.
SI Abdus Sabur of the Dhaka Metropolitan Court's Prosecution Division confirmed the matter.
The accused are Hafez Md Zakaria, 35, and Hafez Md Zobayer Ahmed, 20, teachers at Rowajatul Ulum Hafezia Nurani Madrasa in the Jorakhamba area of Rayerbagh.
According to court sources, the investigation officer and Sub-Inspector Amzad Hossain of Kadamtali Police Station produced the two accused before the court and sought an order to keep them in jail. No lawyer appeared on behalf of the accused during the hearing.
The body of 13-year-old Md Naeem Sheikh was recovered from a third-floor washroom of the madrasa on Monday afternoon.
Later that day, the victim's mother Nazma Begum filed a murder case with Kadamtali Police Station against the two teachers. Police arrested them from the madrasa the same night.
According to the first information report (FIR), Nazma's two sons studied at the madrasa, where Naeem was allegedly subjected to repeated physical abuse by the accused teachers.
The FIR states that after learning about the alleged abuse, Nazma sought to withdraw her son from the madrasa, but the teachers refused to issue him a transfer certificate.
It further alleges that at around 1:00pm on Monday, Naeem told the teachers he no longer wanted to study at the madrasa. He was allegedly beaten and forcibly confined before being strangled to death between 1:00pm and 2:30pm, according to the complaint.

item.title: US hopeful Hormuz strait deal will be done ‘today or tomorrow’ after ship hit
item.description:
The United States was hopeful that a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz would be done “today or tomorrow,” a top US official said Tuesday, hours after yet another cargo ship was hit in the vital waterway.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told broadcaster CNBC “there is a chance we may have a deal” in the coming hours, a day after President Donald Trump said the strait might reopen on Tuesday.
Speaking from the White House on Monday, the US leader continued his now familiar combination of bullish optimism about diplomacy and bellicose threats, warning that this was Iran’s “last chance before decapitation.”
Tehran and Washington have been at war since February 28, when the US and Israel launched surprise attacks on Iran. Despite a ceasefire and a preliminary deal in the months since, diplomacy has failed to end the conflict.
The Strait of Hormuz, a key conduit for global oil and gas supplies, has been the spark for repeated returns to fighting.
Iran wants to maintain control over and charge tolls for the strait, powers it did not exercise before the war and which the US fiercely opposes.
In what has become a regular pattern, Trump last week threatened to hit Iran “very hard,” potentially with attacks against civilian infrastructure, only to pull back on Saturday, saying the “perimeters” of a deal were in place.
On Monday, he said he had agreed to continue to pursue talks with Iran at the request of Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar and other countries.
But Iran’s foreign ministry denied that negotiations with Washington were taking place, even as Trump insisted they were. “We are talking right now,” the US president said.
Qatar, which has been mediating negotiations, said on Tuesday that diplomatic efforts were ongoing but that there were no direct Iran-US talks planned.
Trump said he expected to know by Tuesday how the talks were going, “one way or the other,” but insisted “it’s not very complex.”
The diplomatic focus is on reopening Hormuz, which Trump said could come “literally by tomorrow,” and the denuclearization of Iran, which he said could “take a little while.”
Hours earlier on social media, the president had called Tehran “duplicitous” for saying it was not negotiating.
“Whether Iran wants to admit it or not, we are, in fact, talking of a solution to a problem that they have caused, for decades,” he added.
Trump pointed to the United States’ counter-blockade of Iranian ports, saying: “Nothing gets through to Iran, unless we want it to, and nothing will get through, unless a Deal, or Total Surrender, is accomplished.”
More than five months into a war that has cost Washington billions of dollars, Iran remains able to fire missiles and drones at US and allied targets in the region and retains its enriched uranium stockpiles.
Trump has placed particular emphasis on ending Iran’s nuclear program, which Western nations say is aimed at acquiring atomic weapons. Tehran insists it is a civilian program.
Early on Tuesday, Britain’s maritime security agency Ukmto said a cargo vessel had been struck by an “unknown projectile” in the Strait of Hormuz off the coast of Oman.
The vessel was not named and authorities were investigating, Ukmto said, without offering information on damage or injuries.
Iran continues to impose an effective blockade on the strait and insists ships coordinate crossings with it and take a route that hugs the Iranian coast.
Many vessels have instead chosen to take a southern route, close to Oman on the opposite side of the strait.
Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei has said Tehran is negotiating a new route with Muscat, but that this was not about reopening Hormuz.

Court orders fresh CID probe into Primeasia Student Parvez murder
item.description:
A Dhaka court on Tuesday ordered the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) to carry out a further investigation into the murder of Primeasia University student and Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal leader Zahidul Islam Parvez.
Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Md Sefatullah passed the order after hearing a protest petition (naraji) filed by the complainant against the police charge sheet.
The court directed the CID to submit its investigation report by September 7, state prosecutor Harun-or-Rashid said.
Parvez, a Textile Engineering student at the Banani-based private university, was fatally stabbed during a clash between students of the Textile Engineering and English departments shortly after 4:00pm on April 19 last year.
The following day, the victim's cousin, Humayun Kabir, filed a murder case with Banani Police Station.
After completing the investigation, Banani Police Inspector AKM Moin Uddin submitted a charge sheet to the court on April 29, accusing nine people, including two women.
The charge-sheeted accused are Meheraj Islam, Abu Johor Giffari alias Piyas, Md Mahathir Hasan, Md Al Kamal Sheikh alias Kamal, Alvi Hossain Junayed, Al Amin Sani, Fatema Tahsin Oishi, Faria Haque Tina and Rakib.
The investigating officer, however, recommended the discharge of eight other accused, including Sobhan Niaz Tushar, joint convener of the Anti-Discrimination Student Movement in Banani, citing insufficient evidence.
The others recommended for discharge are Maruf Miaji Hridoy, Rifat, Ali, Fahim, Sakib, Nasim and Nibir.
Humayun Kabir challenged the recommendation by filing a protest petition, alleging that the investigation was incomplete and flawed.
Advocate Mohammad Afzal Hossain Mridha represented the complainant during Tuesday's hearing, while Harun-or-Rashid appeared for the prosecution.
After hearing both sides, the court ordered the CID to conduct a further investigation into the case.

item.title: Two killed in separate road accidents in Dhaka
item.description:
Two people were killed and two others injured in separate road accidents in the capital early Tuesday.
Badda Police Station Sub-Inspector (SI) Md Mahbub Alam said three friends were riding a motorcycle towards the Middle Badda U-loop Bridge at around 2:30am when another motorcycle coming from the opposite direction collided with them and fled the scene.
All three riders were rescued and taken to hospital. One of them, Hasan, who sustained critical injuries, was taken to Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH), where doctors declared him dead at around 3:30am.
The two other injured riders were admitted to the National Institute of Traumatology and Orthopaedic Rehabilitation (NITOR), commonly known as Pangu Hospital.
Hasan was the son of Md Munna of Mirjanagar Alabari village in Begumganj upazila of Noakhali. He worked as a ride-sharing driver and lived in the South Banasree area of Dhaka.
In a separate incident, an unidentified woman was killed after being hit by a bus in the Staff Quarter area of Demra at around 4am.
Demra Police Station SI Mahbur Rahman said police rescued the woman from the roadside and took her to DMCH, where she was declared dead at around 5:30am.
Police said the woman, believed to be around 30 years old, appeared to be a vagrant who often stayed in the area. Her identity has not yet been established.
The body has been sent to the DMCH morgue for an autopsy.

item.title: Adviser Zahed: Media defying court order on Hasina speeches to face action
item.description:
The government will take necessary action against any media outlet that publishes or broadcasts speeches by former prime minister Sheikh Hasina in violation of a court order, Prime Minister's Information and Broadcasting Adviser Dr Zahed Ur Rahman said on Tuesday.
"The government earlier issued an advisory for the media in this regard. If any media outlet announces in advance that Sheikh Hasina will deliver a speech and then publishes or broadcasts it, it will amount to defying the court order," he said at a press briefing held at the Secretariat.
He said the government would once again remind all media outlets to refrain from such activities, stressing that complying with court directives is the responsibility of every individual and institution.
"The government's responsibility is to ensure implementation of the court's decisions," he added.
Expressing his personal opinion, the adviser said he would not have supported restricting the broadcast of Hasina's speeches had there been no court order.
"If anyone disagrees with the court's order, they have the right to challenge it before the court. But as long as the order remains in force, everyone must comply with it," he said.
Replying to a question on why the government came to know about former IGP Benazir Ahmed's bail two to three days after it was granted, Zahed said he was not confirmed about the matter and could not provide an immediate explanation.
Responding to another question on whether the previous government's influence still exists in the administration and other institutions, the adviser said the fall of Sheikh Hasina's government and her departure from the country on August 5 marked a significant event in Bangladesh's history. However, he said it is not possible to replace all officials who served at different levels of the administration during the previous 15 years overnight.
"Many people associated with the previous government are still working in different institutions, including the administration. It is simply not possible to remove such a large number of people at once; the process takes time," he said.

item.title: PM meets experts, assures cooperation for safe water management
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Monday assured experts and representatives of relevant organisations of the government’s cooperation in ensuring safe and sustainable water management as part of its commitment to environmental protection and sustainable development.
He made the assurance while exchanging views with experts and representatives of organisations working in the water, environment and engineering sectors on the country’s water management challenges and possible long-term solutions.
The meeting was held in the Prime Minister’s Office at Bangladesh Secretariat, said PM’s Deputy Press Secretary Hasan Shiplu.
He said the discussion focused on restoring canals, ensuring the stability of rivers and embankments, improving urban drainage systems, wastewater treatment and rainwater management.
The experts and representatives also stressed the need for integrated and effective urban planning to address the challenges posed by rapid urbanisation.
Led by Footsteps Bangladesh, experts from the environment, water and engineering sectors, along with representatives of several organisations working in the field, attended the meeting.
They shared their experiences and recommendations on the country’s water management challenges, existing limitations and possible solutions.
The experts recommended adopting short, medium and long term plans, expanding the use of modern technologies, strengthening coordination among relevant agencies and taking effective measures in view of the impacts of climate change.
After hearing the experts' views and recommendations, the Prime Minister assured them of the government's support to ensure safe and effective water management for citizens in line with its commitment to sustainable development and environmental protection, said Hasan Shiplu.
State Minister for LGRD and Cooperatives Mir Shahe Alam, Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister ABM Abdus Sattar and BNP Special Secretary Belayet Hossain, among others, were present.
The experts and representatives include Footsteps Bangladesh Trustee and Head of Partnerships Fasbeer Eskander, President Shah Rafayat Chowdhury, Vice-President Mohammad Taqi Yasir, former Chief Engineer of the World Bank’s Waste Management Project Tariq Bin Yousuf , Professor Mujibur Rahman of United International University, Red Orange Director Alok Kumar Majumdar, Deputy Director Samiul Islam, Youth for NDC Executive Director Amanullah Parag, GarbageMan founder and CEO Fahim Uddin Shuvo and urban and rural planner SM Mehedi Hasan.
