Bangladeshis can renew iqama with another employer: Saudi minister
item.description:
Saudi Arabia has allowed Bangladeshi migrant workers to renew their iqama (residency permits) under another employer if their original kafeel (employer) fails to renew it, a Saudi minister said on Tuesday.

Saudi Deputy Minister of Labour Market Policies, Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development Muhannad bin Ahmed Al-Essa said that from now on, if the original kafeel of a Bangladeshi worker in Saudi Arabia fails to renew the worker's iqama for any reason, the worker will be able to renew the iqama under another kafeel as quickly as possible, and there will be no legal obstacle to doing so.

He also assured that if detailed information about Bangladeshi workers imprisoned in Saudi jails is sent through diplomatic channels, the Saudi government will give due consideration to granting them clemency.

Saudi Deputy Labour Minister Muhannad bin Ahmed Al-Issa made the remarks during a courtesy call with Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment Minister Ariful Haque Chowdhury at the latter's office in Dhaka on Tuesday, which was also attended by Saudi Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs for Consular Affairs Mohammed AM Alshammari, says a press release of the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment.

The press release said, at the meeting, Dhaka requested the renewal of two of the three agreements signed between Bangladesh and Saudi Arabia on the recruitment of workers—the Domestic Workers Agreement and the SVP Agreement. It was also stated that the recently signed workers' recruitment agreement has been approved by Bangladesh and has been sent to the Saudi government for approval.

Bangladesh requested that a meeting of the Joint Technical Commission be held to discuss various issues related to worker recruitment, training and welfare between the two countries. It also proposed the establishment of a Saudi-Bangladesh Joint Technical Training Centre in Bangladesh as a joint initiative to enhance workers' skills, provide Arabic language training, impart knowledge on Saudi laws, culture and customs, and offer pre-departure orientation.

Bangladesh also proposed developing a framework for the mutual recognition of technical, vocational and professional qualifications to facilitate the recruitment of skilled, highly skilled and professional workers in key sectors such as healthcare, construction, information technology and hospitality.

At the same time, it requested that the timely issuance and renewal of work permits (work visas) and iqama (residency permits) for Bangladeshi workers be ensured. Bangladesh also sought the Saudi government's cooperation in addressing delays by some employers in issuing or renewing work permits, citing the increased work permit fees.

Thanking the Saudi delegation, Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment Minister Ariful Haque Chowdhury said Bangladesh and Saudi Arabia enjoy long-standing friendly relations.

He said Bangladeshi workers are contributing to Saudi Arabia's overall development while also playing an important role in Bangladesh's economy through the remittances they send home.

The minister also noted that students of Qawmi madrasas are highly proficient in Arabic and urged the Saudi side to create employment opportunities for them in Saudi Arabia by providing them with appropriate training.

During the meeting, State Minister for Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment Md Nurul Haque called on Saudi Arabia to recruit more skilled workers from Bangladesh to meet the increased demand for labour ahead of the 2034 FIFA World Cup to be hosted by the Kingdom.

He also urged the Saudi authorities to ensure the rights and protection of female domestic workers from Bangladesh.

At the meeting, Secretary of the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment Md Mokhter Ahmed called for Bangladeshi workers imprisoned in Saudi jails to be granted clemency ahead of the upcoming holy month of Ramadan and Eid.

In reply to Bangladesh's proposals, Saudi Minister Muhannad bin Ahmed Al-Issa expressed strong interest in recruiting skilled and professional workers from Bangladesh in key sectors, including healthcare, construction, information technology and hospitality. He said the Wage Protection System (WPS) and insurance coverage have already been introduced to protect workers' rights.

Muhannad bin Ahmed Al-Issa also assured that if detailed information about Bangladeshi workers imprisoned in Saudi jails is sent through diplomatic channels, the Saudi government will give serious consideration to granting them clemency.

Also present at the important bilateral meeting were Saudi Ambassador to Bangladesh Abdullah Jafar H Bin Abiah, Special Assistant to Prime Minster Shakirul Islam Khan, and senior officials of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment.

item.title: Become Bangladesh ambassadors in India: Dinesh Trivedi tells ICCR scholarship recipients
item.description:
High Commissioner of India to Bangladesh, Dinesh Trivedi, has congratulated the latest cohort of Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR) scholarship recipients from Bangladesh for the Academic Year 2026-2027, and urged the young scholars to be the  ambassadors of Bangladesh and India, in India.

The High Commissioner encouraged the youngsters to  use the opportunity to study in India, not only to excel in their respective fields, but also to explore India, build lasting friendships and serve as connectors between Bangladesh and India, says a press release of the Indian High Commission in Dhaka.

Trivedi was addressing the ‘Send-off’ ceremony hosted by the  High Commission of India, Dhaka to bid farewell to the students selected for the prestigious ICCR scholarships, on 4 August at High Commission premises.

The event was attended by over 120 students from Dhaka, who will be shortly traveling to India to pursue graduate, post-graduate and doctoral courses, ranging from Engineering to Fine Arts, and from Pharmacy to Music, in some of the premier institutes in India.

This year, 541 students from all over Bangladesh have been awarded the ICCR scholarships; out of which 500 students received the prestigious Subarno Jayanti scholarship to pursue graduate, post-graduate and doctoral courses in both STEM and non-STEM streams.

38 students received the  Lata Mangeshkar Dance and Music scholarship to pursue dance, music and culture related courses in India.

Three students were further awarded the ICCR’s QUAD scholarship enabling them to pursue under-graduate STEM courses in India.

Over 7700 applications were received from all over Bangladesh for the ICCR scholarship this year, and 541 students were selected after a round of proficiency test and interview conducted by High Commission of India, Dhaka and other Assistant High Commission of India offices in Bangladesh.

Meanwhile, addressing the scholars, the Indian High Commissioner reminded that only 6 per cent of those who applied have been able to get the ICCR scholarship.

He added that India is awaiting these scholars with open arms, and that studying in India will give a wonderful opportunity to enjoy the diversity of India.

He thanked the parents of the scholarship recipients for nurturing these brilliant minds and placing their trust in India for higher education.

ICCR scholarship is a flagship programme of the Government of India for meritorious Bangladeshi nationals to pursue undergraduate, post graduate and PhD  courses in top tier institutes of India, in various streams, including Engineering, Science, Literature, Humanities and Fine Arts.

The fully paid scholarship provides a unique opportunity for students to study at world class institutes like Indian Institute of Technology (IIT), National Institute of Technology (NIT), Delhi University, Vishwa Bharati University, University of Mumbai, Anna University, etc.

Recipients of ICCR scholarships do not have to pay any tuition fees or any other University fee, and in addition they receive a monthly stipend from ICCR to cover daily expenses.

item.title: Sheikh Hasina's event: Jaiswal says India has no connection
item.description:
The Indian government has no connection with former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina’s participation in a private event in New Delhi or with any views she may express there, according to India's Ministry of External Affairs.

The ministry said the Government of India has no involvement in the event scheduled for Wednesday.

Speaking at the ministry's weekly media briefing in New Delhi on Tuesday, spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal outlined the government's position in response to questions about Sheikh Hasina's planned participation.

Jaiswal said the event in question is being organised by a private media organisation and that the Indian government has "no connection" or involvement with it.

He added that the government neither approves nor endorses any views that may be expressed at such events.

Responding to the same question in Hindi, Jaiswal reiterated that the Government of India has no "connection" with the event.

He said the government does not "support" whatever may be said there and has no "relationship" with the programme.

According to media reports, Sheikh Hasina is scheduled to participate virtually in an event of foreign journalists at the Foreign Correspondents' Club (FCC) in New Delhi on Wednesday.

The event has drawn objections from the Bangladeshi government. On Monday, Bangladesh's Foreign Affairs Adviser to the Prime Minister, Humaiun Kobir, conveyed the government's concerns to Indian High Commissioner Dinesh Trivedi in Dhaka.

Humaiun Kobir requested that Sheikh Hasina and other leaders of the Awami League, whose activities have been banned in Bangladesh, refrain from making political statements while staying in India.

He said such statements could hinder positive progress in bilateral relations and sought India's cooperation on the matter.

According to the FCC, the event is scheduled to run from 6:00 pm to 7:30 pm on Wednesday. Sajeeb Wazed is expected to join virtually from the United States. While the organisers had initially said Sheikh Hasina would participate live via video, they announced on Tuesday that she would instead deliver a pre-recorded audio message. FCC sources also said several fugitive Awami League leaders may attend the event in person.

Sheikh Hasina fled to India after being ousted from power during the mass uprising on 5 August, 2024, and has remained in New Delhi since then.

Bangladesh's International Crimes Tribunal has sentenced her to death for crimes against humanity related to the killings of protesters during the suppression of the uprising. Bangladesh has been requesting India to extradite her to face trial.

During an earlier briefing, Jaiswal had been asked about an invitation extended to Bangladeshi Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to attend the BRICS Summit.

At Tuesday's briefing, he was asked whether the invitation was extended in his capacity as Bangladesh's prime minister or as chair of BIMSTEC.

Jaiswal replied that Tarique Rahman had received a formal invitation to visit India when he became Bangladesh's prime minister in February 2026. The separate invitation to attend the BRICS Summits outreach session, however, was issued in his capacity as BIMSTEC chair.

He said this follows established practice, noting that leaders of other regional groupings had also been invited in their respective capacities.

Jaiswal was also asked about renewing the Ganges Water Sharing Treaty after an Indian parliamentary committee recommended taking steps toward its renewal.

He said Bangladesh and India share 54 transboundary rivers, and decisions on water sharing are handled through the Joint Rivers Commission, along with various bilateral mechanisms and technical-level committees that facilitate discussions on the Ganges treaty.

He added that any talks on renewing the agreement would proceed through these established institutional mechanisms.

item.title: PM: People’s desire for change made July Movement successful
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Tuesday said the July-August Movement became successful because the people wanted change, asserting that its success belonged to the country’s people rather than any individual or political party.
“The movement that took place in Bangladesh during July and August was entirely a people’s movement. The July Movement succeeded because the people wanted change. The movement succeeded only when the people became fully involved in it,” he said.
The Prime Minister was addressing a discussion titled “Seventeen Years of Relentless Struggle for Democracy and the Bloodstained July Awakening”, organized by Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) at the Krishibid Institution Bangladesh (KIB) in the capital on Tuesday afternoon.
Tarique Rahman, also chairman of Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), said people from all walks of life made the movement successful through their active participation.
He said, “We have made our position absolutely clear that the credit for the success of the July Movement belongs to the people of this country. It is not the achievement of any individual or any single political party.”
The Prime Minister said people of the country, BNP leaders and activists and many other political parties that believe in democracy had remained on the streets over the past 17 years in the movement against fascism.
“We never left the field. We never abandoned the people by walking away from the field,” he said. Calling upon all political parties to focus on rebuilding the country, Tarique Rahman said enough discussions, movements, struggles and debates had taken place.
“Now is the time to rebuild the country. Now is the time to move the nation forward. Now is the time to remain patient and vigilant against those who seek to hatch conspiracies,” he said.
The Prime Minister continued, “We must alert the people and gradually implement the commitments we have made to them for rebuilding the country. We must fulfill the people's aspirations.”
Turning to the government's reform initiatives, the Prime Minister said the BNP's 31-point state reform programme had evolved into a national agenda after receiving the people's mandate in the last general election.
"BNP was the first to present a blueprint for state reforms under the leadership of Begum Khaleda Zia," he said, adding, "It was later developed into the 31-point agenda through discussions with our allies on the streets."
In the last election, he said, the people gave their full confidence and mandate to this 31-point agenda. As a result, it is no longer the BNP's agenda alone; it has become the 31-point agenda of the entire nation, he said.
Speaking about the government's performance since assuming office, Tarique Rahman outlined the challenges it inherited and the measures taken to address them.
He said, "After assuming office on February 17, we found that every sector of the country had been left in ruins during the previous 17 years of authoritarian rule."
Sixteen billion US dollars had been siphoned out of the country every year, he said, adding, "The present government began its work amid a fragile economy, a weakened healthcare system and a divided administration."
"Immediately after assuming office, despite various international and regional challenges, the government took prompt measures to ease people's suffering," he said.
On employment generation, the Prime Minister highlighted initiatives to create jobs at home and expand overseas employment opportunities.
He said, "The ban on Bangladeshi workers going to Malaysia has been lifted. Work is also underway to establish large industrial zones in Chittagong and Narayanganj, where Chinese and Korean investments will come."
At the same time, he said, around 50 closed BTMC mills and factories are being reopened under private management, creating employment opportunities for thousands of people.
"Special funds have also been introduced at different levels, including Dhaka University, to support young entrepreneurs," added the Prime Minister.
Referring to the health sector, he said, "Over the next five years, every Upazila Health Complex will be upgraded from 50 to 101 beds. Within the next two to three years, every upazila hospital will have at least a 10-bed dialysis unit. Expansion of dialysis facilities at district and medical college hospitals is already underway."
"We have made heart stents, dialysis, eye lenses and IT equipment more affordable for ordinary people by reducing duties and taxes in the budget," said the Prime Minister.
On education, the Prime Minister stressed reforming the learning system and guiding young people in the right direction. "We want to redesign the education system around the concept of 'Learning with Happiness'. We must understand what our children want and create the right path for them," he said.
He also reiterated the government's commitment to public welfare. "Shaheed President Ziaur Rahman and Begum Khaleda Zia always thought about the development of the country and its people. Following that legacy, the present government is equally committed to serving the people."
Emphasising the need to protect the younger generation from drug abuse, the prime minister stressed expanding sports and cultural activities across the country.
“Recently, football competitions involving 22 lakh primary school children and the ‘Notun Kuri sports competition’ for children aged between 12 and 14 have been organized,” he said, adding, “The government’s goal is to create the right opportunities for young people to develop their talent and potential.”
Referring to the people’s key aspirations, Tarique Rahman said the government was working to fulfill their expectations through sustained efforts.
“Common people want peace on the streets, quality education for their children, better healthcare, security, and opportunities for employment or business according to their abilities,” he said.
“At the same time, citizens want to exercise their political and democratic rights in a timely manner. The government is making every effort to translate these aspirations into reality,” he added.
Reaffirming the government’s commitment to those who were victimised during the July Movement, the prime minister said the government would continue to stand by them and their families.
He said, “During the July Movement, leaders and activists of the BNP, other political parties and countless non-political citizens suffered. The government and the party are standing by the affected people to the best of our ability and will continue to do so.”
He added, “Those who need medical treatment will receive proper healthcare, while those in need of employment will be provided with job opportunities.” Concluding his speech, the Prime Minister prayed for the eternal peace of the souls of those martyred in the 1971 Liberation War, various pro-democracy movements and the July Movement.
He also called upon all to work together to ensure lasting peace, economic progress and a durable democratic order in the country.
BNP Secretary General and Minister for LGRD and Cooperatives Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir presided over the discussion.
Nagorik Oikya Convener Mahmudur Rahman Manna, Jatiya Party (Kazi Zafar) President Mostafa Jamal Haider, Bangladesh Jatiya Party (BJP) Chairman Barrister Andaleeve Rahman Partho, Gono Forum Executive President Advocate Subrata Chowdhury, Revolutionary Workers Party General Secretary Saiful Haque, State Minister for Planning Zonayed Abdur Rahim Saki, Gono Odhikar Parishad President and State Minister Md Nurul Haque Nur, National People's Party Chairman Dr Fariduzzaman Farhad, Jamiat-e-Ulama-e-Islam Secretary General Mufti Mohiuddin and Bhasani Janashakti Party Chairman Sheikh Rafiqul Islam Bablu took part in the discussion.
BNP Publicity Secretary and State Minister for Fisheries and Livestock Sultan Salahuddin Tuku conducted the event. Leaders of Dhaka North and South BNP, Jubo Dal, Swechchhasebak Dal, Krishak Dal and Chhatra Dal also spoke on the occasion.

item.title: Tonu murder accused Hafizur released on bail
item.description:
Retired army member Hafizur Rahman, the only person arrested in the murder case of Comilla college student Sohagi Jahan Tonu, was released from Comilla Central Jail on Tuesday after securing bail from the High Court.
He was released at 7:05pm after all required formalities were completed, Senior Jail Superintendent of Comilla Central Jail Mohammad Shah Alam Khan confirmed.
The jail authorities released Hafizur at 7:05pm after receiving the High Court's bail order and completing all necessary procedures, he said.
The High Court bench of Justice Zafar Ahmed and Justice Sathika Hossain granted Hafizur bail on Sunday following a hearing.
The Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI), which is investigating the case, arrested Hafizur from his residence in Keraniganj, Dhaka, on the night of April 22—nearly 10 years after Tonu was murdered.
He was produced before a Comilla court the following day, when the PBI sought a seven-day remand to question him. Comilla Senior Judicial Magistrate Mominul Haque later granted a three-day remand.
Investigation sources said the PBI collected Hafizur's DNA sample after his arrest and sent it for forensic examination. The DNA report has since been submitted to the court.

item.title: FM says Saudi-led coalition reflects Dhaka’s maritime commitment, regional stability
item.description:
Foreign Minister Dr Khalilur Rahman on Tuesday reiterated Bangladesh's commitment to freedom of navigation, noting that the country's participation in the Saudi-led Multinational Maritime Defence Coalition (MMDC) reflects its commitment to safeguarding international maritime trade routes and regional stability.
The foreign minister held bilateral talks with the vice minister for Foreign Affairs of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, Eng Waleed El-Khereiji, at the State Guest House Padma, where the two sides exchanged views on the evolving situation in the Middle East.
The meeting also reviewed cooperation in security, investment and multilateral affairs, including Saudi Arabia's support for Bangladesh's election as president of the 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly.
Dr Khalilur expressed Bangladesh's solidarity with the Kingdom, appreciated Saudi Arabia's prudent leadership in promoting regional stability, and reaffirmed Bangladesh's support for the peaceful settlement of disputes through dialogue and international law.
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam, Prime Minister’s Foreign Affairs Adviser Humaiun Kobir, among others, were present at the meeting with the Saudi delegation led by the vice minister for Foreign Affairs.
The Saudi vice minister paid a two-day official visit to Dhaka, leading a high-level Saudi delegation that included two deputy ministers and other senior government officials.
Welcoming the Saudi vice minister, the foreign minister reaffirmed that Bangladesh attaches the highest importance to its longstanding brotherly and strategic partnership with Saudi Arabia and proposed elevating bilateral relations to a "Comprehensive Partnership" encompassing political, economic, security and people-to-people cooperation.
The Saudi vice minister highlighted the strong people-to-people ties between the two countries and stressed the need to expand cooperation, particularly in investment.
He expressed Saudi Arabia's interest in investing in Bangladesh's ports, infrastructure and renewable energy sectors, and emphasised the early convening of the third Foreign Office Consultations and the 15th Bangladesh-Saudi Arabia Joint Commission Meeting in Dhaka.
The foreign minister expressed appreciation for Saudi Arabia's continued humanitarian and political support for the Rohingyas sheltered in Bangladesh and requested continued support for their safe, voluntary and sustainable repatriation to Myanmar.
The meeting reaffirmed the shared commitment of Bangladesh and Saudi Arabia to further strengthening their longstanding friendship and expanding their strategic partnership for the mutual benefit of both countries.
Foreign Minister Dr Khalilur Rahman holds talks with Saudi Deputy Foreign Minister Eng Waleed El-Khereiji at State Guest House Padma on Tuesday, August 4, 2026. Photo: UNB
The Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (KSA) has expressed strong interest in broadening its engagement with Bangladesh beyond the traditional manpower sector, with investment opportunities in fisheries, food, energy, renewable energy, information technology and artificial intelligence.
"They (KSA) have repeatedly said the same thing: they do not want to be in just one sector; they want to work with Bangladesh in many sectors," State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam told reporters at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, referring to the visiting Saudi delegation's message.
Shama Obaed said the Saudi side conveyed its confidence in Bangladesh's government following the country's democratic election and reaffirmed its commitment to deepening bilateral ties.
She said the discussions were "very successful and fruitful," with both sides focusing on expanding economic cooperation.
"The Saudi government is interested in investing in Bangladesh by utilizing its expertise in various sectors, including fisheries, food, energy, renewable energy, solar energy, information technology (IT) and artificial intelligence," Shama Obaed said.
She also said Saudi Arabia is interested in recruiting more skilled workers from Bangladesh, describing the issue as another important area of discussion.
"We thanked them because, with the full cooperation of the Saudi government, we were able to bring back our brothers who died there," she said, recalling that three Bangladeshi nationals were killed during the recent conflict in the region. The Saudi delegation paid tribute to them.
The Saudi crown prince has already invited Prime Minister Tarique Rahman. Bangladesh has also invited the Saudi crown prince to visit Bangladesh.
Shama Obaed expressed hope that a joint Bangladesh-Saudi investment meeting would be held soon, with participation from the Bangladesh Investment Development Authority (BIDA) and other stakeholders.
She also announced that political consultations and a Joint Working Group meeting between the two countries are expected to take place in Bangladesh later this year. "This communication and exchange will continue," she said.
Describing the visit as highly productive, Shama Obaed said Saudi Arabia expressed confidence that bilateral relations would continue to grow stronger.
"This visit was very fruitful and, in the coming days, they have also expressed their strong belief that Saudi Arabia-Bangladesh relations will be further strengthened under the leadership of the prime minister," she said.
Responding to a question about a possible visit by the prime minister to Saudi Arabia, Shama Obaed said the visit would definitely take place at a suitable time, based on discussions between the two countries.
Asked whether issues related to Rohingya passport documentation in Saudi Arabia or the illegal stay of some Bangladeshi workers were discussed, she said those matters did not feature prominently in the talks.
"Look, we have the same passport-related problems in all countries," she said.
"Our Bangladesh missions in Jeddah and Riyadh are already working to resolve those problems by maintaining close contact with the Saudi authorities," she added.
Saudi Ambassador to Bangladesh Dr Abdullah Zafer H bin Abiyah recently said they expect greater emphasis on strategic investments, industrial partnerships and technology transfer, noting that the next five years could represent a "transformative phase" in Bangladesh-Saudi economic relations.
"Bangladesh offers one of the most dynamic investment destinations in South Asia, with a market of more than 170 million people and a strategic location connecting South and Southeast Asia," the ambassador said in an interview with UNB.
Traditionally, the partnership has been driven by manpower cooperation and energy trade.
Particularly promising sectors include energy infrastructure, LNG, oil refining, healthcare services, pharmaceuticals and food security initiatives, Ambassador Dr Abdullah said.

item.title: PM says govt working to resolve gas, power crisis without making excuses
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Tuesday acknowledged the hardships people are facing due to ongoing gas and electricity shortages, saying the government is not trying to make excuses but is working continuously to resolve the problems through both immediate and long-term measures.
Speaking at a discussion to mark the 2nd anniversary of the July mass uprising, he also detailed a series of initiatives to increase gas supply and restore electricity generation disrupted by years of neglect in the sector.
"We are not trying to evade our responsibility by making excuses. The problems exist. We know that, and we want to address them," the prime minister said.
The BNP organised the discussion titled "Seventeen Years of Relentless Struggle for Democracy and the Blood-soaked July Awakening" at the Krishibid Institution Bangladesh (KIB) in the capital, with its Secretary General Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir in the chair.
Tarique Rahman acknowledged that people across the country are facing hardships due to shortages of gas, electricity and fuel, saying the crisis has affected households and industries because of the country's battered economy and years of mismanagement in the energy sector.
He said rebuilding a sector that had been "devastated by years of looting" will naturally take time.
The prime minister alleged that the previous "fascist" government had treated the energy sector as a means of plundering, leaving it in a fragile state after years of corruption and mismanagement.
Despite the challenges, he said, the government is making every effort, using its experience and expert advice, to bring the country out of the crisis.
Tarique Rahman said discussions have already begun with neighbouring Myanmar to import natural gas to help ease the shortage.
He also said Bangladesh is in talks with Malaysia's state-owned energy company Petronas to import liquefied natural gas (LNG) through a container-based transportation system.
Recalling his recent visit to Malaysia, the prime minister said he discussed the issue with Petronas and recently spoke directly with Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim seeking cooperation.
He said Petronas held a virtual meeting with Bangladeshi officials on Monday evening and discussions have progressed well.
Although the company already has a long-term commitment with Japan, it is trying to arrange LNG supplies for Bangladesh by October, Tarique Rahman said.
"If we can ensure gas supply to our industries, it will significantly improve the situation," he said.
The prime minister said the government is also trying to arrange gas supplies for around eight power plants that are currently unable to operate because of fuel shortages.
"If gas can be supplied to those plants, about 4,000 megawatts of electricity can be added to the national grid within three to four hours," he said, describing the current problems as the result of years of neglect and poor planning.
Tarique Rahman alleged that the Bangladesh Petroleum Exploration and Production Company (BAPEX), responsible for exploring the country's oil and gas resources, had been virtually paralysed over the past 17 years, with exploration work left largely to foreign companies.
To reverse the situation, he said the government has already decided to procure two drilling rigs for BAPEX so it can accelerate exploration in areas with potential gas and oil reserves.
The exploration process is already underway and, although it will take some time, the prime minister expressed hope that the country will see positive results in the near future.
He said ensuring uninterrupted supplies of electricity and gas is among the expectations of people who struggled and sacrificed for the country over the years, including those who took part in the Liberation War, democratic movements and the July uprising.
Tarique Rahman reaffirmed the government's commitment to restoring stability in the energy sector and reducing people's suffering through sustained reforms and investment.
The discussion was also addressed by leaders of the BNP, its associate organizations and political allies that participated in the simultaneous movement.

item.title: Campuses being turned into ‘havens of terror’ again, alleges Nahid
item.description:
National Citizen Party (NCP) Convener and Chief Whip of the Opposition Nahid Islam on Tuesday alleged that Bangladesh's educational institutions are once again being turned into “sanctuaries of terror”, claiming a familiar pattern of campus and hall grabbing is being repeated.
“Today, an attack was carried out on Jagannath University's Central Students’ Union representatives and the leadership of Chhatra Shakti. Chhatra Dal is trying to take control of various educational institutions, including Dhaka College and Dhaka Alia Madrasah. In Habiganj, our brother Alif had his eyes gouged out,” he said.
Nahid was addressing a discussion titled “From Resistance to Victory: Legacy of July” at Aftabnagar in the capital, organised by the combined private university unit of Jatiya Chhatra Shakti to mark the 2nd anniversary of the July uprising.
Urging the government to learn lessons from the past, he said authorities should avoid getting into confrontations with students and instead allow them to pursue their studies without disruption.
The NCP leader also called for preserving the democratic culture of educational institutions and ensuring employment opportunities for students.
“This government seems to believe that since it is in power, it can seize everything. Sheikh Hasina had thought the same, and you have all seen the consequences,” he said, drawing a parallel with the ousted former prime minister.
Highlighting the contribution of private university students to the July uprising, the opposition chief whip described their role as a “trump card” of the mass movement, saying the authoritarian government had never anticipated that private university students would take to the streets in such numbers.
“After the crackdown on July 17, everyone thought there was no one left to carry the movement forward. We remember the sacrifices of private university students with deep respect. Their role needs recognition and proper documentation. Unfortunately, this government has taken no initiative regarding private universities,” he said.
Among others, NCP Spokesperson Asif Mahmud Shojib Bhuyain, political council member Ali Ahsan Zonaed, Joint Member Secretary Rafe Salman Rifat, Jatiya Chhatra Shakti President Zahid Ahsan, and General Secretary Abu Baker Majumder, along with other private university leaders, spoke as special guests at the discussion.

item.title: Govt urges media not to broadcast statements by convicted fugitives
item.description:
The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting on Tuesday urged all media outlets to refrain from publishing or broadcasting statements by convicted fugitives. The appeal came in a press release issued on Tuesday night.
According to the release, the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) had earlier imposed a ban on the publication and broadcast of statements by former prime minister Sheikh Hasina, who was convicted in a July-August massacre case and remains a fugitive.
The ministry said the tribunal's directive reflects the spirit of the July Mass Uprising. It noted that the ICT instructed the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, the ICT Division and the Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulatory Commission (BTRC) to ensure that Sheikh Hasina's statements are not broadcast, to remove previously circulated hate speech by the convicted fugitive from all platforms, and to prevent its further publication or dissemination.
The release said the National Cyber Security Agency (NCSA) has also requested the media outlets not to broadcast statements by the convicted fugitive, citing relevant legal provisions and the need to protect national security.
Expressing concern, the ministry said that although many media outlets have complied with the tribunal's directive in keeping with the spirit of the July Mass Uprising, some outlets continue to publish or broadcast statements by the convicted fugitive.
The government reaffirmed its respect for the spirit of the July Mass Uprising and the sacrifices of those who lost their lives, while thanking media houses that have refrained from carrying Sheikh Hasina's statements.
It again called on all media platforms, including television channels, newspapers, online news portals and social media, to avoid publishing or broadcasting any statements or remarks by Sheikh Hasina in compliance with the ICT's directive and relevant laws.
The government expressed hope that all media outlets would continue to act responsibly and remain united in upholding national unity and the spirit of the July Mass Uprising.

item.title: DB Chief: No specific threat ahead of Aug 5, DMP on high alert
item.description:
Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) has no specific intelligence suggesting any sabotage plot surrounding Wednesday's observance of July Mass Uprising Day, but has placed the capital under maximum security, Additional Commissioner (Detective Branch) Md Shafiqul Islam said on Tuesday.
Replying to a question while briefing reporters at the DMP Media Centre in the afternoon, he said the police have taken all necessary security measures as the day is considered important.
"So far, we have no specific information regarding any act of sabotage centring on August 5. However, the DMP has taken all necessary security measures. There are various programs scheduled across the city, and adequate security will be ensured for all of them," Shafiqul said.
Responding to another question about Tuesday’s clashes among political parties in the capital, he said differences of opinion among political parties are natural and may sometimes lead to clashes. "However, such incidents should not be viewed as acts of sabotage," he said.
On the recent recovery of bomb-like objects in different parts of the country, the DB chief said the Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime (CTTC) unit is investigating those incidents, while the Detective Branch is also conducting a parallel investigation.
He said there could be attempts to create instability, spread panic among the public or portray Bangladesh as a country linked to militancy, adding that the authorities are investigating the matter with due importance.

item.title: Swapon: Feb-12 election least controversial in Bangladesh's history
item.description:
Information and Broadcasting Minister Zahir Uddin Swapon on Tuesday said the February-12 election was the least controversial among all parliamentary polls held in Bangladesh.
"In Bangladesh, 13 parliamentary elections were held. The most recent election was the least controversial of them all," he said while addressing a discussion, marking the 2nd anniversary of July Mass Uprising at the Council Building of the Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (Buet) here.
The minister said Bangladesh has not attained the desired institutional framework for the executive, judiciary and legislature yet.
“But we cannot say we have reached the place of our desired judicial system. Even in the light of the thought based on common democratic values, we have not yet achieved the institutional structures required for the executive branch, the judiciary, the legislative branch of the state,” he said, claiming that Bangladesh has never passed through a stable socio-economic system.
Referring to the 2024 July Mass Uprising, Swapon expressed optimism that the aspirations created following the sacrifices made by the martyrs of the July Uprising will enter a final stage, so that the country's socio-economic system will never again have to fall into this constraint.
He said if the country truly wants to achieve such a desired state, it must first understand why these repeated instabilities occurred and whether the root causes have been removed.
“If we try to look at July Mass Uprising from a research perspective, then we will truly be paying our respects to the martyrs of July Uprising,” he said.
Buet Teachers' Association President Prof Muhammad Anisuzzaman Talukder chaired the discussion, while Buet Pro-Vice Chancellor Prof Mohammad Shariful Islam attended it as a special guest.
Former Buet pro-VC Prof Abdul Hasib Chowdhury and Dean of the Faculty of Civil Engineering Prof Md Abdul Jalil were present as guests of honour in the event.

item.title: Renowned folk singer Mujib Pardeshi lands in jail
item.description:
A Dhaka court on Tuesday sent renowned folk singer, composer and music director Mujib Pardeshi to jail in a Tk10 lakh cheque dishonour case.
Dhaka Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Md Sefatullah passed the order after police produced the accused before the court. Idris Ali Biswas filed the case with Magura court in 2022.
On March 15, 2023, the 2nd Joint District and Sessions Judge of Magura Muhammad Anwar Sadat sentenced Pardeshi to one year's rigorous imprisonment and fined him Tk10 lakh, the value of the dishonoured cheque. As he remained absconding, the court subsequently issued an arrest warrant against him. Police from Uttara West Police Station arrested Pardeshi on Monday.
SI Helal Uddin of the prosecution division said police sought an order to keep the accused in custody after producing him before the court. The court ordered that he be sent to jail.
No lawyer appeared on behalf of Pardeshi during the hearing. However, the complainant's counsel Shafiqul Islam opposed bail, arguing that the accused had remained absconding despite being aware of the case and had shown disregard for the legal process. He urged the court to reject the bail petition, saying Pardeshi's release could prejudice the complainant's interests.
Mujib Pardeshi, whose real name is Mujibur Rahman Molla, is a renowned Bangladeshi folk singer, composer and music director. He rose to prominence in the 1980s with his Bengali folk and traditional songs.

item.title: People in Gazipur plant paddy seedlings on unfinished road
item.description:
Residents of Sreepur upazila in Gazipur planted paddy saplings on an unfinished road protesting the prolonged suspension of a development project after the contractor allegedly abandoned the work nearly two years ago.
The protest was held on Monday on a two-kilometre stretch of the Nayanpur-Barmi road, where construction work has remained incomplete, causing severe suffering for thousands of commuters.
The six-kilometre road connects residents of Gafargaon and South Gafargaon upazilas of Mymensingh with Sreepur’s Kawraid, Barmi and Telihati unions. Locals said the damaged road has disrupted the movement of industrial workers, students and residents in the area.
The Local Government Engineering Department (LGED) awarded the road improvement contract to Messrs Shammi Enterprise under the 2024-25 GOB Maintenance Project-3. The project, funded by the government’s revenue budget, was estimated to cost Tk4.09 crore.
The work, which started in mid-2024, involved repairing the road from Nayanpur Bazar to CCDB Mor. However, after digging up the road and laying brick chips, the contractor stopped work and has remained absent from the site, according to locals.
A visit to the area found that the road has developed numerous potholes as the brick chips were washed away over time. Rainwater has accumulated in several places, making the road hazardous for vehicles and pedestrians.
Local traders Rakib Mia, Sultan Uddin and Mostafa Kamal said the road becomes almost unusable after rainfall.
“After rain, it becomes difficult to tell where the road ends and the potholes begin. People fall, vehicles get stuck, and businesses are suffering,” they said.
Auto-rickshaw driver Sumon Mia said he has been unable to operate on the road for nearly two years, resulting in a significant drop in his income.
“A few weeks ago, some workers were seen at the site, but now all work has stopped. No one from the contractor’s side can be found in the area,” he said.
Local physician Shamsul Islam Tarek said residents had welcomed the repair initiative when it began but are now facing greater difficulties.
“Before the repair work started, we could still use the road. Now travelling has become extremely difficult. We urge the administration to take immediate steps to complete the work,” he said.
Attempts to contact Ziaur Rahman, owner of Messrs Shammi Enterprise, were unsuccessful as he did not respond to repeated phone calls.
Sreepur Upazila Engineer Touhid Hasan said the authorities had repeatedly notified the contractor to resume work but failed to get a response.
“Considering public suffering, we have informed higher authorities about imposing penalties and cancelling the work order. A fresh tender process will be initiated soon,” he said.
He blamed the contractor’s negligence for the delay and said the project would be completed after cancelling the existing contract and appointing a new contractor through a fresh tender.

item.title: US hopeful Hormuz strait deal will be done today
item.description:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said that the United States could reach a deal with Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz by Wednesday, adding that this would stabilize energy prices.
“We are in talks with the Iranians, and I think there is a chance we may have a deal today or tomorrow to open the strait and move towards a more normalized position in this conflict,” Bessent said Tuesday in an interview with CNBC.
Asked if a deal would allow Iran to charge a toll on shipping using the strait, Bessent said: “I think it would be freedom of movement.”
Bessent’s comments echoed those of US President Donald Trump on Monday, who insisted the waterway could reopen within hours after he pulled back from threats of a massive military strike on Iran over the weekend.
Iran’s foreign ministry has denied that negotiations with Washington were taking place, and on Tuesday, an unknown projectile hit a cargo ship in the Strait of Hormuz, a key point of tension in the US-Iran conflict.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Tuesday the United States is “involved” in negotiations between Oman and Iran on increasing traffic through the strait, through which around 20% of global oil shipments passed prior to the war.
“There’s been progress made in those talks but not finality yet; we’re hoping that will happen very shortly,” the top diplomat told journalists.
Bessent was upbeat on the impact a deal with Iran over the strait would have on energy prices, where he said hundreds of ships are waiting to go out.
“Even though things are still a little dicey there over the past few days, we’ve (seen) quite a few ships coming out even now,” Bessent said.
“So you know, I’d expect the energy prices to settle back down, which, as I said, will be good for the entire world.”

item.title: Death toll in Spain’s Ceuta from migrant rush hits 75
item.description:
Last week’s irregular entry of tens of thousands of migrants from Morocco to Ceuta left 75 people dead in the Spanish north African territory, officials said on Tuesday, raising the toll from 72.
The Spanish government’s delegation in Ceuta confirmed the figure to AFP after the rush from July 30 saw many migrants drown as they tried to swim around a barrier in the Mediterranean Sea.
Morocco’s interior ministry on Sunday said 11 people died on the Moroccan side of the border, all but one by drowning.
Spain says 70,000 of the 72,000 migrants who reached Ceuta have returned to Morocco.
Those who remain face squalid living conditions with limited access to shelter, food, water and sanitation, AFP reporters in Ceuta saw.

item.title: Japan sees need to boost military with ‘sense of urgency’
item.description:
Japan needs to boost its military with a “sense of urgency and crisis,” its defense minister said Tuesday, as a new government assessment again highlighted growing risks from China, North Korea and Russia.
Japan is already beefing up military spending and security cooperation in Asia, deploying missile launchers to outer islands, moving to acquire “counter-strike” capabilities, and easing rules on weapons exports.
But Shinjiro Koizumi said in a preface to the annual defense white paper that it was “imperative that Japan further reinforce and transform its defense capabilities with a stronger sense of urgency and crisis than ever before.”
In the Asia-Pacific “not only are China and North Korea further strengthening their military capabilities, China-Russia and Russia-North Korea are also reinforcing their cooperation,” he added.
The white paper said China was “intensifying its activities” in the region around Japan, “extending beyond the so-called first island chain to the second island chain.”
The document listed a series of incidents in 2025, including activities by Chinese aircraft carriers and the “unusual close approach” by Chinese aircraft to Japanese planes in two incidents in June and July.
A spokesman for China’s defense ministry said the white paper was “filled with false narratives.”
“This is a classic case of shifting the blame onto others, and an excuse to loosen (Japan’s) own military constraints,” said Chen Xi, according to an online post by the defense ministry.
“We strongly disapprove of this,” said Chen, calling on Tokyo to “stop misleading the Japanese people and the international community.”
Japanese jets scrambled 595 times in the year to March 31, 2026, including 366 sorties against Chinese aircraft and 214 for Russian planes.
This compares to 704 the previous year and was the fewest since at least 2021.
Japan decided in April to lift its self-imposed ban on weapons exports, but the white paper highlighted problems in the country’s production base that could jeopardize procurement and innovation.
Koizumi also said that he and US counterpart Pete Hegseth had “exchanged candid views” on the “unwavering” US-Japan alliance, while also increasing security cooperation with the Philippines, Australia and South Korea to realize a “a Free and Open Indo-Pacific.”
“As the security environment becomes increasingly and rapidly severe, what is required now is to strengthen resilience against crises all across the entire Indo-Pacific region,” Koizumi said.
“In order to do so Japan will build and expand multilayered networks among allies and like-minded countries, and enhance interconnectivity with like-minded countries and others in every area.”
China has expressed alarm at what it sees as a return to “new militarism” by Japan, with relations worsening since comments about Taiwan last year by hawkish new Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi.

item.title: Extreme heat costs Asia’s poorest workers health and wages
item.description:
Brijpal Singh spends long hours working construction under the blazing sun in Noida, a sprawling industrial satellite city in India’s National Capital Region. Even as temperatures soar past 45 degrees Celsius (113 Fahrenheit), work on the building site rarely stops.
By the end of each shift, the 51-year-old says his heart is pounding, and he’s usually dizzy, dehydrated and physically drained from hours in the heat. Yet taking a day off is a luxury he cannot afford.
Missing work would mean losing his daily wage of 500 to 600 rupees ($6 to $7, €5.20 to €6.10). The money supports his wife and three children living in a village in Uttar Pradesh, a two-day journey away.
“There are days when I don’t feel like working,” said Singh. “But if I miss a day, who will take care of my children and pay for their expenses?”
Some 5 million people work in the Delhi region’s informal economy, accounting for roughly 80% of the total workforce. And as climate change drives up temperatures, many paid by the day like Singh are faced with an impossible trade-off between providing for their families and protecting their health.
The past decade has been India’s warmest on record, bringing more frequent, intense, and prolonged heat waves. At the same time, heat is reducing productivity and increasing illnesses, with one study finding rising temperatures could be costing informal workers the equivalent of 2% of their country’s GDP annually. That’s nearly $80 billion (€69 billion).
“Wage losses are only going to worsen as temperatures continue to rise,” said Ameena Kidwai, lead researcher at People’s Courage International, a nonprofit aiming to strengthen informal workers’ rights. “Workers are now putting in many more hours than they did before to complete the same amount of work.”
The US-based organization surveyed informal workers in five Asian cities. Kidwai said some of those surveyed reported that tasks once completed in eight hours now take 10 to 12 hours during the hottest months, as they slow down to cope with dangerous conditions.
With heat becoming a major occupational hazard, workers described the harm to their health, ranging from respiratory and gastrointestinal illnesses to stroke and kidney disease.
“As a result, workers also have to spend more on over-the-counter medicines and visits to clinics or hospitals,” Kidwai said.
A lack of ability to recover is a defining feature of urban heat for informal workers — from construction laborers and street vendors to delivery riders — say researchers.
Like Singh, many are migrants who leave their families behind to earn a living in fast-growing cities, said Patricia Samantha Narvaez, a program manager at the Philippine development organization Ideals.
“You would expect home to be a place of relief,” said Narvaez. “But many live in densely packed neighborhoods with poor ventilation, little green space and heat-absorbing concrete.”
That’s the case for Singh, who returns to a single room with poor ventilation after work. During the hot months from April to June, it becomes a furnace, and frequent power cuts make it difficult to cool down before the next day’s shift.
“During the hot days, I can’t eat well,” Singh said. “I often drink oral rehydration solution and go to bed without eating.”
Narvaez surveyed informal workers in Quezon City for a report on the impacts of extreme heat. The city is just northeast of Manila, the capital of the Philippines, a country in which some 42% of the employed population are informal workers.
“Some participants described Quezon City as a ‘concrete jungle’ because even at night it remains unbearably hot,” said Narvaez.
Fifty-year-old Aida Tano has experienced such conditions firsthand. Tano worked in a garment factory in Quezon City for nearly two decades, where soaring temperatures, heat-generating machinery and poor ventilation turned the production floor into an oven. With no air conditioning, four workers shared one electric fan.
“There was no escape from the heat,” Tano said. “We complained, but management told us that if we couldn’t endure it, we could leave.”
Narvaez says it’s not unusual for factory owners to restrict measures that help workers cope with the heat even for trivial reasons such as not wanting fans to break down. At Tano’s workplace, she had to pay for her own drinking water, and even climbing stairs to leave on her break became too exhausting in the heat.
The factory has since closed, but after a long day in extreme heat, Tano, who now does odd jobs like sewing and cleaning, would come back to a house with no AC. She still relies on electric fans and keeping windows covered to block the sun, both of which do little to cool her home.
The economic impacts of climate change hit women hardest, largely because they account for a majority of the world’s poor, according to the United Nations.
Women in the informal economy also shoulder a disproportionately large burden because they combine paid work with unpaid caregiving responsibilities, said Ameena Kidwai of People’s Courage International.
“They’re managing their jobs while also running their households,” Kidwai said. “When children or older family members fall sick during a heat wave, the caregiving duties fall largely on women.”
Shanti Devi, a 36-year-old daily wage laborer in Noida, has been her family’s sole breadwinner since her husband was injured in a workplace accident several years ago.
“Now I have to manage the house, care for my children and also try to earn a living,” said Devi.
During heat waves, school closures and a shift to online classes often force Devi to stay home with her four children instead of going to work. Each day of lost wages adds to the already struggling family’s financial strain.
“I took the day off because it is too hot to work, and my children are home because their school is closed for the summer,” Devi said. “I have to cook for them. When school is open, they eat their meals there.”
Frequent power outages and overheated homes also leave many women up through the night caring for family members in the heat before returning to work the next day. Disrupted sleep and lack of rest come with increased health risks, such as heart disease and diabetes, meaning women are often more vulnerable than men in heat waves.
Researchers say these overlapping pressures expose a gap in many cities’ efforts to adapt to a heating planet. While India has introduced heat action plans, and Quezon City is developing its own measures, protections for informal workers remain limited and unevenly enforced.
As temperatures rise because of human-caused climate change, experts say measures focus largely on short-term responses and often overlook the realities of informal workers’ lives.
“Climate change will only deepen existing inequalities because those with the fewest resources are often the most exposed to extreme heat,” Narvaez said. “Ultimately, resilient cities cannot be built on exhausted and unprotected workers.”
